📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we know Robert Pattinson is on Christopher Nolan’s “nice list” considering he’s cast the actor in two of his movies. (Did you know Pattinson even helped inspire Nolan to make Oppenheimer?) While the pair seem to have a great filmmaking partnership going, there was one time on the set of The Odyssey where Nolan totally rejected one choice Pattinson was hoping for on the spot.

It has been revealed that pattinson, of course, plays the very deplorable Antinous in The Odyssey. Before cameras started rolling, the actor reached out to the hair department to request a long wig for the part. As the movie’s hair department head Gloria Casny told it, when he called she just happened to be standing right next to Nolan. In her words:.

I didn't even know how he got my number… The answer was no.

Sources indicate that that’s right. No conversation or negotiations, just “no”. Casny told the story during a news conference for The Odyssey in promotion of it becoming one of the latest 2026 movies that’s available to watch at home. The story led Matt Damon, who was the event’s moderator, to make this comment:.

It's funny because he knows Chris and he’s worked with Chris… Chris is literally allergic to anything like that.

Sources indicate that I can definitely see Pattinson’s vision for Antinous, but apparently one of Nolan’s rules is he doesn’t like to have actors wear any wigs or fake facial hair. Makes sense for the filmmaker who famously tries to do as much of his movies practically as possible.

Sources indicate that there’s been a few other stories around Nolan and Pattinson that have also come out before. For example, he’s reportedly the only cast member who asked to read the script. Also, Mia Goth told a story about how one time on set Pattinson approached Nolan with a question while they were filming and Nolan simply responded with “That’s your department, mate”. Nolan has a different way of working than most, but that’s got to be one reason he’s considered one of our best living filmmakers.

Pattinson wasn’t the only actor on the set of The Odyssey that made a request to the hair department. As Matt Damon told USA Today during the same event, he had actually asked Nolan if he could have a fake beard to play Odysseus. Can you guess Nolan’s answer? Per Damon’s words:.

Recent findings suggest that he just looked at me like, 'No.’ He’s like, ‘Just grow your beard.’ He likes everything real. To be fair, given the amount of time spent in the ocean and water alone, the hand-laid beard would never have worked. Where you’re just out in the elements all the time, it just wouldn’t have made sense.

Same reaction! How funny. Damon really did grow a magnificent beard though, so it all worked out. And, honestly Pattinson’s forward-swept bangs fit perfectly, too. You can appreciate the lack of wigs on The Odyssey by purchasing it for home viewing now.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth Is in a Battle for His Own Survival at the Pentagon

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office.
  • Hegseth was in a precarious position.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be debuted by a member of his own party.

Hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

Recent findings suggest that in the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump revealed the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

Hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” stated Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

The secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official mentioned: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

It was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

Sources indicate that “In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

“They will stand behind him in the short term,” noted a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

The morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

As the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. A US Army sentinel guarding the memorial turned to the group and shouted out a reprimand: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” After video of the moment made for embarrassing headlines, Hegseth awarded the soldier a Joint Service Commendation Medal and posed alongside several Army officers for a photoshoot that was posted on his social media accounts. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” said a former senior defense official.

According to recent reports, the small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” remarked John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

In his latest book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. Jennifer plays an instrumental role in those efforts, directing the secretary’s social media and a small battalion of accounts that support him online. “It was as if she was producing him in his role as Secretary,” Ullyot writes. She has helped produce—and starred in—dramatic videos of Hegseth posted by the Pentagon’s official social media accounts. “Her entire job is to make his image,” one source told Vanity Fair.

House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

In a recent development, her role extended well beyond production, alarming senior officials in the Department of Defense. She interviewed candidates for Pentagon roles. She attended sensitive bilateral meetings with foreign officials. She was included in Signal chats that discussed the war prepares for the Houthi operation in Yemen. The former defense official mentioned they warned Hegseth about his wife’s involvement in Pentagon affairs. “She did not have a fucking clearance,” they said. “She shouldn’t be privy to this shit.”.

Hegseth himself seemed too smitten to care. He covered the walls of his office, as well as other meeting rooms and corridors throughout the Pentagon, with large photos of himself and his wife. When The Latest York Times examined Jennifer’s influence at the department over the summer, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the former cable news producer “an accomplished leader.” He added that the Pentagon “not only welcomes her current leadership but actively plans to involve her even more deeply in the future.” Politico later reported that while advising the secretary of defense, Jennifer was being paid for consulting work by Watchtower Strategies, a Washington lobbying shop that counts Lockheed Martin as a client.

In a recent development, she wasn’t the only Fox News producer at the Pentagon. Hegseth also gave Radabaugh—a former producer on Fox & Friends Weekend with no government experience—broad authority over department affairs, I’m told. Radabaugh made sure that glamorous photos and videos of Hegseth were published online promptly, sometimes scolding aides for taking too long to post. In the first few months of Hegseth’s tenure, she ordered Ullyot to turn a room just off the briefing room into a makeup studio.

Sources indicate that “This was ridiculous. I said not only no, but hell no,” Ullyot writes. He warned that news of the makeup studio would leak. “How exactly did a makeup studio fit into the warrior ethos?”.

It has been revealed that in response to a detailed list of questions, Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez declined to answer many of them but emailed a lengthy statement criticizing Ullyot. “There is no ‘makeup studio’ in the Pentagon, and it never existed,” Valdez noted, going on to call Ullyot “a skinwalker,” a “sour puss coward,” and “generally a stupid person” who left “his job in disgrace.” (According to information reviewed by Vanity Fair, Hegseth praised Ullyot after his departure from the Pentagon and offered to recommend him to Susie Wiles, then Trump’s chief of staff.).

In a recent development, “I volunteered to help stand up the Secretary’s press operation for a few months at the start of his term,” Ullyot told Vanity Fair in response. “I left as planned, and the Secretary thanked me for my work. My record over more than 30 years, including as a senior spokesman in the Senate and in the Trump White House, speaks for itself.”.

Hegseth was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” noted the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.”.

It has been revealed that soon after his confirmation, Hegseth moved to increase his powers and consolidate control over the Pentagon. He ousted generals and subjected senior staff to polygraph tests to weed out leakers, a crusade that resulted in the abrupt firings of top officials that demoralized staff. He tapped Tim Parlatore, his personal lawyer, as a special adviser and charged him with overseeing leak investigations. Parlatore continued to run his own private practice as a criminal defense attorney, and Politico reported this week that while serving as Hegseth’s top adviser, he is representing the son of a Libyan warlord accused of extrajudicial killings and torture.

In keeping with the president’s broad campaign for retribution, Hegseth ordered an investigation into retired Joint Chiefs Chairman General Mark Milley, who had clashed with Trump during his first term, and stripped the four-star general of his security detail. The Pentagon is now working on a latest report on the 2021 Kabul Airport attack, during which 13 American soldiers and 170 Afghan civilians were killed in a suicide bombing during the withdrawal from Afghanistan. At the time, Milley served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The new assessment, one source familiar with the investigation remarked, is expected by the end of the month and is intended to serve as a predicate to strip Milley of his four-star rank.

Hegseth waged a parallel war on the press, starting with an attempt to ban NBC News correspondent Courtney Kube from the Pentagon. In a meeting with his advisers, Ullyot writes, Hegseth explained that he and his wife Jennifer were “angry” at Kube for how much she covered his turbulent confirmation process before Congress. “I thought this was loony tunes,” Ullyot writes. One source told me that after NBC News was kicked out of its Pentagon office, Hegseth aides took a full-length mirror from the vacated room and installed it in his makeup studio.

Industry observers note that as Hegseth purged senior officials, he grew closer to Buria. The relationship was confounding to many inside the building: Hegseth has pushed to cleanse the Pentagon of ideological diversity, yet he elevated Buria, a holdover from the Biden administration who had previously donated to Democrats. But Buria had earned the trust of Jennifer. When explaining to advisers why he was elevated, Hegseth mentioned he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen says he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

Buria was by Hegseth’s side throughout the Signalgate scandal, which, according to several administration officials, was a turning point for the secretary. “Every problem he is having in one way or another goes back to Signalgate,” the second Trump official remarked. “His extremely hostile relations with the press, his paranoia, his firing of certain people, denied promotions to generals. It was all around paranoia related to Signalgate.”.

“There’s two versions of Hegseth,” noted a second former defense official. “There is the pre-Signalgate version and the post-Signalgate version. It’s like Jekyll and Hyde. He was Dr. Jekyll until around Signalgate, and he’s been Mr. Hyde ever since. He’s just not making good decisions.”.

It was an almost unbelievable incident: Hegseth shared war plans for a bombing campaign against the Houthis in Yemen on at least two Signal group chats, including one that inadvertently included Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor in chief of The Atlantic.

This was the first major military engagement of Hegseth’s tenure, but he chose to survey the operation with Buria from a temporary secure facility at his Fort McNair home rather than make the short trip to the Pentagon or the White House Situation Room. The decision alarmed some at the Pentagon. “It’s your first major military operation,” said the second senior Trump official. “Why would you monitor it from your shitty SCIF in your basement? Why not go 10 minutes to the Pentagon where you have the joint staff?”.

“You would think with kinetic operations going on in the Middle East that could have dramatic consequences for service members, that he’d be in the office,” Tillis said.

Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.”.

During Hegseth’s confirmation process, allegations of heavy drinking concerned Republican lawmakers he needed to vote in favor of his nomination. At the time, several Republican senators mentioned he promised them he would stop boozing if confirmed. He affirmed this pledge publicly: “This is the biggest deployment of my life,” he told Megyn Kelly in a 2024 interview, “and there won’t be a drop of alcohol on my lips while I’m doing it.”.

Industry observers note that whether or not Hegseth has actually quit drinking continues to be a source of palace intrigue. One official recalled watching Hegseth drink what the secretary suggested were two cocktails—though the official conceded he hadn’t seen the drinks poured, and raised a theory that Hegseth might have been testing whether he would leak the incident to the press. “This was at a time of peak paranoia,” the official noted.

Recent findings suggest that buria was known to drink on official trips; the official recalled Hegseth’s aide handing out shots to passengers on a US government jet during a Pentagon junket. Two other officials remarked Buria would often brag about drinking with Hegseth, including on an official trip to Panama in 2025. The Fresh York Post later reported that Buria had made up a story about him and Hegseth donning disguises to go out and drink, all in an effort to weed out leakers. One of the officials told me they believed the leak claim was Buria’s retroactive effort to cover up that he was boasting about drinking with the secretary.

Recent findings suggest that “The drinking is what they’re really afraid of,” the second official stated. When asked directly if Hegseth continued drinking as secretary, a Defense Department spokesperson who declined to be named said in a statement: “No, the Secretary has kept his promise that he made during his confirmation hearings and has not drank since becoming Secretary of War.”.

Jennifer and Pete Hegseth have forged a close relationship with Stephen Miller and his wife Katie, their neighbors on a placid and heavily fortified army base south of the White House. Hegseth’s temporary salvation comes thanks in part to support from Miller, who values his deference to Trump. “Stephen doesn’t like all the Liberace shit, the cucaracha shit,” said the first former official. “Pete right now is fresh out of friends, and misery loves organization. But don’t get it twisted. At any moment, at any second, Stephen will cut Pete’s throat.”.

The secretary of defense has made few friends in Washington. One source recalled attending a holiday party stocked with members of the administration during which Hegseth spent much of his time alone in the corner of the room. “Even Kash Patel had people coming up to him to talk,” the source said. “Pete was alone and isolated. He looked depressed. And this was before the Iran war. His stock has not gone up since then.”.

Recent findings suggest that hegseth has channeled much of his effort into appealing to an audience of one, telling advisers he only cares about Trump’s opinion. “The one thing he’s been successful at, and I think it’s the only thing, is flattering Donald Trump constantly,” the former official said.

Recent findings suggest that the purpose of this flattery campaign extends beyond keeping his current job. In private, Hegseth has confided in several officials about his ambitions to run for president. This jockeying has exacerbated tensions with Vice President JD Vance. The relationship was already strained by Vance’s private opposition to the Iran war, and it deteriorated significantly after the vice president’s close friend, Dan Driscoll, was pushed out of his position as Army Secretary in August following months of friction with Hegseth.

When explaining to advisers why Buria was elevated, Hegseth noted he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen notes he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

“Secretary Hegseth and Vice President Vance share an outstanding working relationship grounded in deep mutual respect and alignment,” Parnell stated in a statement to Vanity Fair.

Jennifer has worked in tandem with her husband to push allies on social media and in the press to promote the idea of a presidential run. “She wants to be first lady,” the former official said of Jennifer. “She wants to be Hillary.” After the midterms, online influencers whom Hegseth hired earlier this year to work as special government employees at the Pentagon began pitching Hegseth for president. These influencers were nominally hired to promote Hegseth’s efforts to bring war colleges in line with the “warrior ethos,” but in reality they coordinated with Jennifer and Radabaugh on “shitposting,” the second official said. Earlier this month, they rallied to Hegseth’s defense as he came under fire for the Republican ballot box-bloodbath, posting action shots of the secretary with the caption: “STAND. FIGHT. DEFEND THE REPUBLIC.”.

Recent findings suggest that these influencers often attack journalists who cover the Pentagon. In response to a recent story by Politico’s Daniel Lippman, an active-duty Army officer known as InfantryDort on social media—whom Hegseth hired as one of these shadow spokespeople—posted: “I expect you all to ratio the fuck out of this retard and in short order. Daniel Lippman remains absolute journalistic filth.” A Politico spokesperson responded: “Daniel is one of Washington’s best-sourced reporters, and we’re lucky to have him at POLITICO.”.

It has been revealed that when Democrats take control of Congress, they are expected to focus much of their oversight on Hegseth, including the scandals from his personal life. The subjects broached in his contentious confirmation hearings—including an affidavit signed by his former sister-in-law alleging abuse against his second wife—are likely to be relitigated. (His second wife denied that she was physically abused.).

According to recent reports, “Is that going to be good for the president?” Tillis asked. “His entire confirmation will be re-prosecuted. That affidavit will get a lot of attention. Family members will most likely be subpoenaed. Does he really want to go through that at a personal level, and at the same time be such a massive disruption for the leader of the most lethal, complex organization in American government? Is this about Pete, or is this about America’s defense? I don’t know how any objective person can say that the value that he brings is greater than that distraction and the cost of him remaining in place.”.

In a recent development, “If he had any dignity, he would resign and allow the president to appoint a replacement in the lame duck session,” said the first official. “But he doesn’t.”.

Hegseth’s ability to project confidence is not confined to the cameras. He was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” said the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.” In late December 2025, Hegseth met with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Four Seasons in Palm Beach shortly before Netanyahu ventured to Mar-a-Lago to make the case for fresh strikes on Iran. By February, Netanyahu was pushing Trump to join Israel in a full-blown war to topple the Iranian regime.

Hegseth was all-in, his confidence buoyed by the success of Operation Midnight Hammer—a series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025—and the raid to abduct Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro. His allies in the administration point to these operations, as well as a post-pandemic surge in military recruitment numbers, as his major successes in the job.

But multiple officials who spoke with Vanity Fair noted they believed that when briefing Trump, Hegseth understated the risks of war with Iran from the beginning and went on to overstate its successes as the conflict dragged on. “Pete gave the rosiest picture in the world,” said the first former official. During early discussions about potentially launching the war, the official said they were struck by how quickly Hegseth started speaking about the operation as a “foregone conclusion.”.

“Leading up into the war, he presented, along with [Central Command Commander Admiral] Brad Cooper, overly optimistic projections of what the air campaign could achieve,” remarked the second administration official. “This is how the president got this idea that it could be done in a matter of two to three weeks.”.

Hegseth ran against Democrat U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar in 2012.

Tillis, for his part, mentioned that he did not believe Hegseth was forthright with Trump about the war. “He planned the good, bright, shiny stuff that was Epic Fury, but clearly did not brief the president on things that anybody that’s had any experience in the Middle East knows,” Tillis added. “The first thing that goes is the Strait of Hormuz.”.

“Secretary Hegseth and Pentagon leadership consistently provide the President with the complete, unvarnished picture so he can make the best choices for America’s security and success,” Parnell said in a statement.

On the first day of the war, a missile struck the Minab elementary school in southern Iran, killing more than 150 people, the majority of them children. The US military has thus far refused to publicly admit responsibility for the strike, despite a preliminary military investigation concluding within days of the strike that a US missile struck the school. Before the attack, Hegseth gutted the Pentagon program aimed at reducing civilian harm during military operations, ProPublica reported in March. House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Massie cast the strike as a consequence of Hegseth’s oft-repeated mantra: “Maximum lethality, not tepid legality.”.

Sources indicate that as the war went on, officials mentioned, Hegseth continued to trumpet its successes, showing the president what one official described as “hype videos” depicting strikes on missile launchers, Iranian ships, and old aircraft. Hegseth told Trump “that the majority of Iran’s missile capabilities and the majority of Iran’s Air Force was destroyed,” the official said, even though US intelligence “indicated that wasn’t the case, and that the majority of Iran’s missiles and missile launchers by the end of the major combat phase of the war were still intact.”.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” mentioned Senator Tillis.

Industry observers note that hegseth also worked behind the scenes to promote positive media coverage of the war. He briefed Fox News hosts whom he remained friendly with on the war’s progress and encouraged them to present a positive picture on air. But Hegseth himself has made little effort to explain or defend the war to Americans. Even as the war has become a political debacle for the administration, he remains bullish on escalation. “Pete is the only one who wants to restart strikes,” the first official noted.

It has been revealed that we were all sitting in our assigned seats waiting for the performance to start when a security official walked into the Pentagon briefing room to make an announcement. Hegseth had not held a Pentagon press briefing since May. Now, facing an impeachment effort from a member of his own party, he came before the cameras. “If anyone gets out of line today, you’re going to be physically removed,” the official said. “Is that clear?”.

Industry observers note that “Sense of decorum,” the official noted apologetically. “Just be professional.”.

The official said he was just relaying orders from Hegseth’s office. A few minutes later, Joel Valdez, the press aide, walked out and asked if anyone was confused. Everyone was. “I could tell you off the record?” he said. No, the reporters replied. “Do you want to hear it off the record?” No, they said again.

Recent findings suggest that valdez looked down at his shoes and then walked out of the room without saying another word. “In my 30 years in DC, I have never heard that,” remarked a cameraman. “This is crazytown.”.

Recent findings suggest that at 8 a.m. sharp, Hegseth walked out wearing a loud plaid suit, a striped tie, and an American flag pocket square. The timing is no coincidence; officials remarked Hegseth schedules briefings in the 8 a.m. hour because Trump is known to watch Fox News at that time.

The secretary of defense began reading his speech from a stack of papers on the podium. From my assigned seat in the back row, I felt as if I were watching an interpretive dance. The choreography of Hegseth’s hand movements and facial expressions was as slick as his hair, which was gelled into a stiff meringue that moved in unison with his tanned face.

Hegseth punctuated a line about President Trump’s “decisive” leadership with a clenched fist thrust downward. The word “overseeing” was expressed with a slow swipe of the hand over an imaginary stretch of purview. As Hegseth recalled the glories of the Maduro operation—and, parenthetically, his part in directing them—he dismissed criticism of the raid by leaning into the microphone, shaking his head from side to side and wiggling his eyebrows: “It wasn’t”—dramatic pause for eyebrow wiggle—“a kidnapping.”.

Hegseth's presser had a pantomime quality.

It has been revealed that the briefing itself exuded little of the confidence Hegseth sought to signal before the cameras. He took seven questions in total, sticking to friendly reporters in the front rows who had signed a pledge in September 2025 to not report “unauthorized information” from the Pentagon. One of them, a representative of Real America’s Voice, asked “what message” is sent to America’s allies when “our own politicians don’t support taking out the narco traffickers that kill their own constituents?” It wasn’t so much a question as a warm bath. Some in the room, visibly frustrated by the waste of time, rolled their eyes. Others shouted questions from the back about Iran and impeachment. Hegseth refused to look at them.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” mentioned Tillis, who also decried Hegseth for filming a slick video of himself outside the Department of Defense making the case for why he should not be impeached: “He demonstrated more impulsiveness by using taxpayer dollars to defend himself against impeachment.”.

In his remarks before the press, Hegseth framed the effort to remove him as an attack on the troops. “If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he stated, jabbing a finger into his chest. But the impeachment targeted Hegseth, not “the warriors.” We had assembled to hear Pete make the case for Pete. Indeed, he had not held a press briefing when a Navy commander died in a helicopter crash on July 1, or when three US soldiers were killed in an Iranian strike on a base in Jordan on July 17. What brought him back before the cameras was not the ongoing war in the Middle East but his own fight to save his career here in Washington.

The performance earned a rave review from the one viewer who mattered. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Early on in Hegseth’s tenure, he confided in advisers about his “biggest fear” as he took on the mighty responsibility of leading the Department of Defense, the first former official told me: “Being fired and embarrassed.” For now, Trump is standing by his secretary. He always is, until he isn’t. When asked just before the midterms whether Wiles would remain on as his chief of staff, Trump stated there was “zero chance” he’d replace her. Three weeks later, she was out.

10 Books Like ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ You Should Read Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason.
  • Industry observers note that the story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast.
  • It has been revealed that it’s no shock that one of Sarah J.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sarah J. Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason. A complex heroine who keeps discovering new depths in herself, fascinating supporting characters who shift from antihero to antivillain in unexpected ways, creative and beautifully rendered world-building—the series has it all, while also being unapologetically romantic (and steamy).

Industry observers note that the story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast. If you need more books with the same lush feel, here are 10 to get you started.

It has been revealed that it’s no shock that one of Sarah J. Maas’ other series would be recommended for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses, but there’s a specific reason you should jump into her Crescent City series, especially the third book, House of Flame and Shadow. The most recent ACOTAR book, A Court of Splintered Harmony, revealed that the events of House of Flame and Shadow tie directly into the events in Splintered Harmony, particularly with regard to the character of Feyre’s sister, Nesta. In other words, if you read Splintered Harmony and wondered why Nesta was being so weird, there’s a whole other book series you should dig into immediately.

Industry observers note that if Feyre’s grit and determination are your favorite aspect of ACOTAR, Julie Kagawa’s Iron Fey series (starting with The Iron King) will be your next obsession. Meghan Chase has never felt ‘normal’ in her life, and she’s been haunted by her father’s disappearance since she was a child. When her brother also vanishes, she goes on a quest for answers, learns that she’s actually the daughter of a faerie king, and finds herself in a magical world that blurs in elements of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Meghan is determined to save her brother (and herself), but a certain ice-cold fae prince captures her attention, even though he’s as dangerous as he is beautiful.

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for some serious romance in your fantasy, Jennifer L. Armentrout’s A Blood and Ash series is a must. Poppy was chosen at birth to be the kingdom’s Maiden, isolated and untouched in order to be ready for her Ascension to ensure the land is protected from the evil force that took her family. But it’s a lonely existence—until Hawke is assigned as her sworn protector. Golden-eyed and beautiful, Hawke offers Poppy the connection she’s craved. When chaos erupts around her, Hawke takes the opportunity to spirit Poppy away. But Hawke has a secret, and Poppy is soon in danger of losing both her heart and the favor of the gods themselves.

Sources indicate that if you love how A Court of Thorns and Roses takes the “enemies-to-lovers” trope and builds it into a deep, complex mesh of emotions and plot twists, you’ll love Shelby Mahurin’s Serpent & Dove series. When witch Louise le Blanc flees her coven, she takes shelter in the city of Cesarine, where magic is forbidden, and witches are unceremoniously hunted and burned. Louise’s life gets infinitely more complicated, dangerous, and steamy when she’s trapped into an unwanted marriage with Reid Diggory—who happens to be a huntsman of the Church, charged with tracking down and eliminating witches. And then Louise starts to realize that Reid is actually pretty darn hot.

If you’re looking for a romantasy that’s broadly similar to ACOTAR while being its own thing, read A.K. Mulford’s The Five Crowns of Okrith series, starting with The High Mountain Court. Remy is a red witch, which means she’s in hiding and ready to make a run for it if the fae get near. So when a group of fae shows up at her tavern, she makes for the exit—only to be captured by Prince Hale of the Eastern Court. Instead of striking her down, however, Hale asks Remy for help—he needs to locate two ancient magical artifacts created by red witches, and he needs her red magic to find them. Hale promises to set her free and even reunite her with the red witches still living. More importantly, Remy finds Hale irresistible and has a primal urge to stay with him, no matter what the cost.

Looking for a romantasy with a slightly different vibe from ACOTAR? Variety is the spice of life, after all—and The Fourth Wing delivers. Rebecca Yarros’ Empyrean Series made a huge splash when it debuted, and for good reason—it has everything, from a capable, intelligent heroine thrust into a dangerous scenario (in this case, a dragon rider academy where failure can be deadly) and forced to navigate alliances, conspiracies, and her own heart, which is pushing her towards a romance that might be as dangerous as the dragons themselves.

Love the moral complexity of ACOTAR, where everyone has at least a touch of darkness? Check out The Folk of the Air series by Holly Black. When Jude was a child, the father of her half-sister, the faerie Madoc, murdered her parents and took her back to the Faerie world with him. Raised as part of the gentry, Jude lives in a world where her mortal nature is hated and despised, but she battles for her place at court anyway while struggling with her love-hate relationship with her adoptive father and a growing bond with the titular prince, a relationship that is strictly forbidden. Jude is a fierce and extremely morally gray character, and one that fans of Feyre will adore.

Sources indicate that looking for more smart women at the center of beautifully-rendered fantasy stories? You’ll love Princess Lucero-Elisa de Riqueza of Orovalle, star of this series-starter by Rae Carson. Elisa was chosen for “Service” as a baby, when a godstone was placed in her navel by the gods, signaling that she was destined for greatness. But as a young woman, Elisa is self-hating and miserable. She’s never done anything even remotely great, and spends her time isolated, overweight, and reading military strategy books. One day she’s shocked to discover she’s been married off to the king of a distant land on the brink of war—and suddenly all that rage and book learning becomes invaluable as she struggles to survive an unfamiliar court and help her latest homeland survive a dangerous onslaught.

If you loved Feyre’s journey as she discovered unknown reservoirs of power and courage inside herself, you should read Leigh Bardugo’s Grishaverse novels, starting with Shadow and Bone. As a child, Alina was tested by the Grisha and found to possess no magical ability. As an adult, she serves as a cartographer in the army. Charged with guiding the Darkling—the most powerful of the Grisha—across the dangerous and terrifying Shadow Fold, Alina is unexpectedly revealed to have incredible powers and is packed off to train with the Grisha. There, she must determine who her friends and enemies are, even while falling under the spell of the charismatic Darkling.

Recent findings suggest that emilia di Carlo and her sister Vittoria are very different—Emilia is bookish and shy, Vittoria outgoing and brash—but they share a secret: They’re both streghe, and have spent their lives learning to use magic. In this version of Italy, the Malvagi (the seven princes of Hell) haven’t been seen in a long time, but a terrifying accident summons the Prince of Wrath and leaves three witches dead, including Vittoria. Emilia swears to use her power to avenge her sister, but when her revenge is delayed and she’s forced to work with Wrath, unwanted feelings begin to tick up the spice level to an uncomfortable degree.

Within minutes of iPhone Duo pre-orders opening on October 16, delivery estimates quickly slipped into November, then December, and after about a half hour of orders, the earliest you could get an iPhone Duo was late January.

But as spotted by Max Weinbach, new iPhone Duo orders from Apple just got bumped up by about a month. Now, delivery estimates are showing December 16-23 for customers in the US and elsewhere.

New Duo orders seemed to have been pulled forward ~a month They must be scaling manufacturing quickly pic.twitter.com/VFkCmCoRLF.

  • It has been revealed that early in the game, Cal, a friend of co-protagonist Jason, spends an afternoon gaming with his buddy.
  • As GTA 6’s nearly 20 million players (at the time of this writing) know, GTA 6 is digital-only.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now out everywhere, and players are discovering just how much this game is filled to the brim with an overwhelming amount of things to do. In the game’s opening hours, you’ll land a place on the water, steal a car from a police impound, get into a car chase, and more. There are a million little things to do, like playing video games inside GTA 6 itself.

It has been revealed that early in the game, Cal, a friend of co-protagonist Jason, spends an afternoon gaming with his buddy. Ironically, he does something that IRL players can’t do with GTA 6 itself: bring a physical game disc with him.

As GTA 6’s nearly 20 million players (at the time of this writing) know, GTA 6 is digital-only. “Physical” copies simply contain a digital download code in a box. As such, you can’t bring your copy of GTA 6 to a friend’s house to show them the game like you could with previous GTA games, or like how Cal introduces Jason to Tenebrae Lux, a very artsy game that spoofs Jonathan Blow’s The Witness. (Jason’s not impressed; he’d rather go kill zombies.).

The two then have a party-filled night together that ends with them drunkenly fighting over who gets to sleep in the bed, which then cuts to the both of them sharing the bed in their undies. It’s a surprisingly wholesome sequence that includes Jason opening up about the strains in his relationship with Lucia on the eve of her getting released from prison. The moments of genuine friendship between Cal and Jason contrast well to the rest of GTA 6, which is all about, ya know, stealing drugs from rednecks, evading death-by-gator, running away from cops, and all other kinds of wild shenanigans.

Trading games, bringing a game disc to a hang sesh with the boys, introducing a fresh game to a friend by popping your copy into their console — for years, sharing games was easy because they were all on discs or other physical formats. When I reviewed the Gears of War remaster last year (with a digital copy), it reminded me how I first played the original game by trading my copy of Assassin’s Creed with a friend for his copy of Gears. Fast-forward to this year, and I’m playing Pokémon Pokopia by borrowing my partner’s copy. (OK, maybe I stole it from her Switch 2 case, who can say.).

Recent findings suggest that playStation once famously demonstrated how to share used games in a 2013 video intended as a dig toward the always-online Xbox One. That joke has aged like milk in the wake of Sony’s announcement that it will cease manufacturing physical discs for PlayStation games in January 2028. Sony’s news hit just a short time after Rockstar Games confirmed its own digital-only looks for GTA 6 back in June.

Sony’s move prompted a wave of angry commenters spamming every PlayStation promotional video and blog post with disdain ever since. Some PlayStation owners tried to wrangle together a “no disc, no buy” blackout campaign where they wouldn’t use PSN, make purchases at the PlayStation Store, or basically engage with their PlayStation console in any way. That blackout had no effect on Sony. In fact, Sony’s digital game sales have continued to grow since the announcement.

It has been revealed that the outrage over the decline of physical games clearly hasn’t had an impact on Rockstar’s GTA 6 either. It broke preorder records, despite there being no real need to preorder a copy — they’re all digital, so Sony and Microsoft won’t be running out. This isn’t 2009, when you had to preorder a physical copy of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 to make sure you could pwn some newbz day one. (And snag a sleek poster in the process.).

Sources indicate that though we can’t say with certainty yet, it seems likely GTA 6 will end up as 2026’s top-selling game, in spite of the uproar around its lack of a disc version. Yet none of the eleventy billion people who buy it will be able to share it with their buds in the way that Cal shared a disc version of Tenebrae Lux with Jason.

Industry observers note that following the arrival of Apple Intelligence on iPhones in China with iOS 27.3 beta 1, Apple is now expanding support to iPads and Macs ahead of the public release of its 27.3 updates. Here are the details.

Apple’s road to releasing Apple Intelligence in China has been a particularly eventful one.

After a significant amount of regulatory back-and-forth, the manufacturer confirmed in late October that Apple Intelligence would make its way to iPhones as of iOS 27.3, beginning with the first beta of the system, released in early November.

Just a few days later, Reuters reported that Apple had cleared another regulatory hurdle in the country by registering Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops.

Today, Apple released the second developer betas of iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3, both of which now include Apple Intelligence support in China, as spotted by MacRumors.

As with the initial iPhone rollout in the first iOS 27.3 beta, Apple Intelligence on iPads and Macs in China does not include Siri AI or the other next-generation AI features announced at WWDC 2026.

Instead, users get access to earlier capabilities such as Writing Tools, Genmoji, Live Translation, and notification summaries, with Alibaba’s Qwen model powering certain features.

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" broke box office records, cementing Spidey as a reliable draw at a time when most other superhero movies aren't bringing in the crowds like the used to. Now, Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures have decided to re-release the movie for the holiday season, complete with previously unseen footage that will reintroduce a cut Daredevil crossover. We just got a sneak peek at that same crossover via a picture posted to Claire Temple actor Rosario Dawson's Instagram.

Temple originally appeared in Netflix's "Daredevil" series before becoming a mainstay in that small-screen universe. The nurse not only tended to Charlie Cox's Daredevil but also his fellow Defenders: Krysten Ritter's Jessica Jones, Mike Colter's Luke Cage, and Finn Jones' Iron Fist. (Temple didn't appear in Jon Bernthal's "The Punisher" series.) Alas, the Netflix series were all canceled by early 2019. Since then, Cox's Matt Murdock has returned in the Disney+ show "Daredevil: Born Again," in addition to making a brief cameo in 2021's "Spider-Man: No Way Home.".

Sources indicate that originally, "Brand Upcoming Day" also featured a crossover with the erstwhile Netflix "Daredevil" series. Sadly, a scene that featured Temple was removed from the final cut prior to its debut in July 2026. Now, however, that scene has been reinstated for the extended cut, awkwardly titled "Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day," which hits theaters on December 4, 2026.

Per The Hollywood Reporter, "Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day" features 10 minutes of extra footage, most of which remains a mystery. One thing we do know, however, is that Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple cameo has been reinstated.

Industry observers note that the actor took to Instagram to post a photo from the scene in question, which shows Temple standing alongside Tom Holland's Spider-Man inside a hospital room. This clearly takes place at the end of the movie, following Spidey's tumultuous final showdown with Sadie Sink's Jean Grey. Beyond that, however, Dawson didn't reveal much about what happens in the footage. "So excited to enjoy this record-breaking movie on the substantial screen," she wrote in her caption."[...] with an extended cut of new scenes and surprises... Ahhhh!".

Recent findings suggest that dawson previously revealed how she felt about being cut from "Brand New Day," saying that she had a BTS post ready to go about her time on-set that she ultimately had to scrap. Clearly, the actor was disappointed, which isn't surprising considering "Brand New Day" absolutely ruled the box office. Still, as she said at the time (via Variety) "Because everybody's in it, it still means that my character is somewhere in that same universe, and I really love that. So, I hope I get to be Claire again." Now, with her footage being added back into the movie for the re-release, she has even more reason to be hopeful.

With Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple appearing in the "Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day" re-release, the question becomes whether she'll show up again as the Marvel Cinematic Universe enters its next phase. As of now, "Daredevil: Born Again" has been canceled at Disney+, which means the upcoming third season will be its last. Thus far, Claire Temple hasn't appeared in the revival series, but there have been a few oblique references to a friendly nurse. Whether she'll show up in "Born Again" Season 3 remains unclear, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did.

Sources indicate that with the show having been axed, however, Temple's MCU future remains even more uncertain. Perhaps if we get a fifth Tom Holland Spidey outing, she might come back. But such a film is also yet to be confirmed. "Brand New Day" producer Amy Pascal has one rule for making another movie, which essentially amounts to focusing on one film at a time. Still, with "Brand New Day" becoming nothing short of a phenomenon, it seems almost certain Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios will want to get Holland back for another outing ASAP.

According to recent reports, indeed, "Brand New Day" has made $2.5 billion at the global box office, and the re-release will likely bring in a decent bit of extra profit. Hence, with "Born Again" ending after its next season, a "Brand New Day" sequel seems like the most likely venue for a Temple return. For now, though, we'll have to await further news.

Survivor's coin flip remains a controversial addition to the game, as fans debate the pros and cons of what it brings to the CBS series. I initially didn't have issues with what went down with Lewis Kelly in Season 51's flip, until I learned there was more than one flip involved.

It has been revealed that lewis spoke to Rob Has A Podcast about his exit and was asked if he'd pick water over fire if he flipped the coin again in a future season. The third juror revealed that he didn't have to think about the hypothetical, because he flipped the coin twice the night of his elimination. Hear the story below:.

In a recent development, well, here's the thing. I did actually do it once [before the one shown] and it didn't land in the circle, and I hear 'fire.' And maybe I should've changed it. I didn't think about it, so, it's tough.

According to recent reports, lewis had to flip the coin twice, and the first time it landed on fire! Lewis didn't say how he felt about that, but I can say that as a Survivor fan, I'm pissed.

Survivor 51's Kilby Lost All Of His Worldly Possessions After A Wild Storage Wars Scheme Went South.

Industry observers note that I went back and watched Survivor, and Jeff Probst noted that the contestant who correctly called the coin flip won immunity, an idol, and the grand prize went up another million. The only rule was that it had to land on what he called. At no point was it said the coin had to land on the mat, which wasn't even used for the shot of Lewis' coin flip.

Jeff's word is law on Survivor, and if he's allowed to push contestants to admit they like fire challenges on-camera, he should've honored the result of the initial coin flip. Obviously, they faked it for the camera that he took the flip a second time on camera. They should've stuck with his original flip result and just filmed until he recreated it in the way they wanted it shot.

To me, multiple flips for the coin feel sketchy. Sure, Lewis had a 50/50 shot both times, and one flip didn't impact the outcome of the other. At the same time, Lewis won the first flip and had it negated by something that wasn't part of the rules. Is it then fair that his odds of survival went back to 50% for a redo?

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Now, there's also a third option here in which the mat and all of that was explained to Lewis ahead of the flip, and maybe that's why he wasn't as bent out of shape as I am. I'll also admit he was one of my favorites, so I'm also sad about seeing him head to the jury before this season wraps up on the 2026 TV schedule.

Recent findings suggest that survivor's Open Era continues to be full of surprises, which certainly keeps both the contestants and viewers on their toes. I think the biggest disappointment with this coin flip is that the payoff was pushed to next season. Right now, all we have to fester on is disappointment, and the fact that someone threw away their chance to stay in the game on a coin flip. We'll see what happens next Wednesday, and how Lewis' exit will impact the group dynamic.

These Are the Best Ways to Encrypt Your Email

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft).
  • In a recent development, as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server.
  • Emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like Gmail (Google) or Outlook (Microsoft). But if you are sending sensitive information via email, you can minimize what can be snooped on and by whom using end-to-end encryption, which generally ensures that only the recipient can read your message. Here's what you need to know about email encryption and how to set up an extra layer of privacy.

In a recent development, as this in-depth explainer from Adaptive Security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via Transport Layer Security (TLS), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server. However, encryption is temporarily stripped at each server: content is received and processed in plaintext and then re-encrypted when it leaves, meaning it could be read, logged, and distributed by the server provider.

Emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on Google's servers and in a Gmail recipient's inbox. But this only prevents someone with physical access to the server hardware from reading messages, as Google still holds the encryption key and can access stored data. And, as PCMag points out, Google is scanning your messages to a degree, and it (along with other email providers) can and will hand emails over to law enforcement and government agencies in some cases.

In a recent development, by contrast, with end-to-end encryption (E2EE), emails are readable only on the sender's and recipient's devices, and can be decrypted only with the recipient's private key. They're never translated into plaintext as they pass between and through servers to their destination, meaning that no one—including server providers, hackers, or law enforcement—can view the content. It's worth noting, though, that E2EE is not impenetrable nor a total guarantee of privacy. For example, metadata like subject lines and email addresses may remain in plaintext, and encrypted messages are still susceptible to phishing. Plus, forwarding an encrypted message breaks the encryption.

Still, end-to-end encryption is especially useful when sending sensitive information that may be valuable to bad actors, though if security and privacy are a high priority, you may want to consider it for all of your emails. How you deploy encryption depends on whether you are adding it to your current email or switching to a dedicated provider.

If you have an account with a major email provider like Gmail, Outlook, or Apple Mail, you can add a third-party tool that layers an encryption protocol like OpenPGP on top of your existing account. PCMag recommends PreVeil, SecureMyEmail, and Virtru (which is limited to Gmail people in Chrome) for those who want to keep their current emails. Mailvelope is a browser add-on (and therefore a desktop-only tool) available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, though it can also be installed on other browsers, like Brave, that are built on the same architecture. FlowCrypt integrates with Gmail and Google Workspace on desktop and mobile.

Recent findings suggest that note that enterprise owners of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 have access to true end-to-end encryption without third-party add-ons. Gmail's Confidential mode and Outlook's Encrypt feature, available to all users, are not E2EE equivalents, as Google and Microsoft, respectively, still manage the keys.

For those who are willing to start fresh with a new email address (or who have a custom domain), providers like Proton Mail or Tuta offer native end-to-end encryption. The caveat: by default, this is only between users on the same service, so from one Proton user to another. If you want to send an end-to-end encrypted email from Proton to a Gmail user, for example, you have to set up password protection (and share the password via another secure channel) or use a PGP-compatible tool like those listed above. You can also Proton's Gmail integration does allow for end-to-end encryption, but only if both Gmail parties are using the Proton integration.

The bottom line here is that email wasn't designed to be a highly secure form of communication. End-to-end encryption does add a layer of privacy and security if you jump through hoops to set it up, but it's still susceptible to human error and social engineering.

Apple TV today celebrated two Grammy nominations, one of which further establishes a canceled show as an unlikely awards success story. Here are the details.

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

In a recent development, ‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 latest songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027. To check out the full list of nominees, follow this link.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV demonstrates and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google and OpenAI are going head-to-head again, and this time, their newest AI models arrived just five days apart.
  • Industry observers note that google rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, promising faster responses, stronger reasoning and better performance across everyday tasks.
  • It has been revealed that both companies are making massive promises about what their AI can do, but benchmarks and launch demos only tell part of the story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google and OpenAI are going head-to-head again, and this time, their newest AI models arrived just five days apart.

Industry observers note that google rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, promising faster responses, stronger reasoning and better performance across everyday tasks. Then, on November 17, OpenAI fired back with GPT-6.2 Astra, its latest model designed to tackle everything from complex research and writing to coding and creative projects.

It has been revealed that both companies are making massive promises about what their AI can do, but benchmarks and launch demos only tell part of the story. What matters is how these models perform when you actually put them to work.

So I put Gemini 4 Hydrogen and GPT-6.2 Astra through the same five real-world challenges to see which one delivers better results, where each struggles and which AI is actually worth using.

Prompt: You're an event coordinator managing a one-day technology conference with 120 attendees, three meeting rooms and six speakers.

Sources indicate that the conference runs from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Each speaker must deliver one 45-minute presentation. Every presentation requires a 15-minute room reset afterward.

Speaker A is available only before noon.

Speaker B cannot present before 11 a.m.

Speakers C and D must not present at the same time.

Speaker E must present immediately after Speaker A, in the same room, allowing for the required room reset.

Speaker F is available only between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m.

All attendees must have a shared lunch break from noon to 1 p.m.

Each room can host no more than three presentations.

A 30-minute keynote involving all six speakers must take place at 4:30 p.m.

Sources indicate that create a complete conference schedule showing start times, end times, room assignments and speakers. Identify any conflicts and explain how you resolved them. Do not change any constraints without explicitly stating why.

GPT-6.2 identified both keynote conflicts, and it also identified the exceptions that would need approval. This directly addresses the instruction not to change constraints without explaining why. It correctly scheduled the six individual presentations and demonstrated reset periods explicitly and preserved the shared lunch break.

In a recent development, hydrogen was strong on presentation and the mechanics of the individual talks. Its table is easy to follow, with resets alongside each presentation. It also correctly handles the A-to-E sequence, B’s earliest start, C and D’s separation, F’s individual talk, lunch, and room limits. It also explains why the selected times work for the individual presentations.

Winner: GPT-6.2 wins on constraint reasoning and transparency. Hydrogen offers a solid schedule, but it mistakes fitting the individual presentations into the day for satisfying the entire conference specification.

Prompt: Write the opening 500 words of a literary mystery novel. A woman arrives at a small coastal town to attend the funeral of someone she has never met. Everyone in town recognizes her, but nobody will explain why.

Write in first person, past tense.

Start with a sentence of exactly seven words.

Include a conversation that sounds natural but contains a hidden threat.

Establish a distinctive setting without using a long descriptive paragraph.

Introduce one seemingly insignificant object that becomes notable in the final sentence.

Do not use the words "mysterious," "secret," "shadow," or "dark.".

End with a revelation that changes how the reader understands the opening.

Sources indicate that avoid clichés, melodrama and obvious AI-generated prose. Prioritize believable characters and original storytelling.

GPT-6.2 delivered an opening sentence that satisfies the seven-word rule and it introduced the identity question without explaining it. The narrator feels like a believable person and the setting emerges through activity. The threatening conversation retains plausible deniability. Alan’s questions about whether anyone expects her back could be concern or an assessment of how easily she could disappear. “If you get a signal” sharpens that uncertainty. That stated, the ending is overcompressed.Hydrogen provided a clear, accessible opening with an easy-to-follow progression from ferry to town to diner. Its opening sentence also contains exactly seven words: “The morning ferry docked at eleven sharp.” It maintains first-person, past-tense narration and avoids the prohibited words. Hydrogen’s main weakness is that the final revelation does not sufficiently change our understanding of the opening.

Winner: GPT-6.2 wins for an ending that makes the reader reconsider what already happened. Hydrogen’s ending mainly makes the reader wonder what happens next. Both can create suspense, but GPT-6.2 answers this prompt more successfully.

Prompt: Build a fully functional, interactive website called "Decision Lab" that helps people compare difficult choices.

Customers should be able to enter up to five options, define their own decision criteria, assign importance weights from 1 to 10, and score each option against every criterion.

Automatically calculate weighted scores and rank the options.

Display a visual chart comparing the results.

Let customers edit or delete options and criteria.

Include a sensitivity analysis showing whether the winner changes when the most key criterion's weight is reduced by 50%.

Include a "What if?" feature that lets users adjust weights and immediately see updated rankings.

Provide three realistic sample decisions that users can load instantly.

Save user changes between sessions if the environment supports persistent storage.

Use a modern, polished interface with intuitive controls. Every button and calculation must actually work.

Don't create a static mockup. Build the functioning app, then test its calculations and interactions. Explain any limitations.

Sources indicate that GPT-6.2 built and published an interactive website for comparing up to five choices. I simply enter what matters, give each criterion a weight, and score the options. The site ranks them and updates the chart as changes are made. It also added a “what if?” slider section to experiment without changing original weights.

Hydrogen built a self-contained, responsive web application and tested its calculations and controls before displaying it. It also build a scoring matrix, added support for up to 5 options and implemented live calculations and charting.

Winner: GPT-6.2 wins for a more thorough and useful website. The interactive site followed the prompt exactly while also adding extras that were useful for the overall project.

Prompt: You're the operations manager of an independent bookstore.

It's 4 p.m. on Friday, and the following problems happen simultaneously:.

Recent findings suggest that A bestselling author is arriving at 5 p.m. for a signing attended by 80 customers.

The shipment containing 60 copies of the author's book is delayed until Monday.

You have only 12 copies in stock.

Your only experienced employee just called in sick.

A customer claims they were charged twice for a $75 purchase, but your payment system is offline.

A local journalist is asking whether the store is experiencing financial difficulties.

Your landlord has emailed demanding an overdue $2,000 payment by Monday.

You have $900 in available business cash, two inexperienced employees and one hour before the event.

Develop a realistic action plan.

Rank problems by urgency, explain what you would do in the first 15 minutes, write a short statement for customers attending the signing, and draft a response to the journalist.

You cannot cancel the event, invent money, pretend books have arrived or promise refunds that you cannot verify.

It has been revealed that be transparent without creating unnecessary panic. Explain what information you still need before making irreversible decisions.

GPT-6.2 treated the task as several connected operational problems, rather than simply a shortage of books. It prioritized safe event operations and gave inexperienced staff narrow roles. It checked capacity, kept exits clear, and assigned responsibility for the queue to better manage 80 attendees without the experienced employee.Hydrogen was practical in several aspects. But it promised to put bookplates into books “as soon as the boxes arrive Monday.” That turns the expected shipment date into a firm fulfillment commitment. Overall, the model introduced several unsupported assumptions — and its customer statement promises arrangements that its own proposal states still need confirmation.

In a recent development, winner: GPT-6.2 wins as the stronger operations-manager answer because it preserved options while keeping customers, staff, the author and the landlord informed. Hydrogen had useful ideas but repeatedly moved from “ask whether this is possible” to “tell customers this will happen.”.

Prompt: Five researchers, Ava, Ben, Chloe, Daniel and Elena, each work on a different project (robotics, climate, medicine, astronomy and cybersecurity), use a different programming language (Python, Rust, JavaScript, Go and Julia), and work on a different floor (1 through 5).

Determine each researcher's project, programming language and floor using these clues:.

The robotics researcher works on floor 5.

The person using Rust works exactly one floor above the climate researcher.

Ben works on a lower floor than Chloe.

The astronomy researcher uses Julia.

The cybersecurity researcher works on floor 1.

Elena works exactly two floors below the robotics researcher.

The medicine researcher uses Python.

Chloe does not work on robotics or climate.

The JavaScript user works on floor 2.

The climate researcher works on floor 2.

Produce a complete table showing every researcher's floor, project and language.

Explain whether the clues produce exactly one solution, multiple solutions or no solution. If the puzzle is inconsistent or underdetermined, identify the problem rather than inventing an answer.

GPT-6.2 followed the prompt’s most notable instruction. It identified inconsistency rather than inventing a complete assignment and it provided three clear ways to demonstrate the problem.Hydrogen reached the same correct conclusion and explained the same underlying problems. It successfully identified three contradictions and flagged the Floor 3 collision between Ava and Elena, the project–language mismatch on Floors 3 and 4 (medicine/Python and astronomy/Julia vs. Rust and Go), and Chloe being forced onto Floor 1 with no lower floor available for Ben.Winner: Hydrogen wins narrowly on clarity, accuracy and presention.

Recent findings suggest that google and OpenAI are competing to become your everyday AI assistant, but how each one handles tasks can make all the difference. In this experiment, GPT-6.2 won nearly every test, which might just make it one worth paying for. Hydrogen is free and did a decent job answering each prompt, but often struggled with assumptions and adding details. For people hoping to keep costs down, Hydrogen is still a good choice, you'll just want to do some extra fact-checking and evaluate the model's response a little closer than you would with GPT-6.2. Overall, GPT-6.2 proves to be a strong model for taking on every day tasks thoroughly, accurately and quickly. Have you tried these models yet? Let me know in the comments what you think of each one.

The reviews are in for Joe Biden’s new book, Promise Me, America. The Atlantic calls the book “unrepentant.” The New York Times calls it a 400-page “cover letter.” The former president offers the fantastical opinion that he should have stayed in the race in 2024 and faced Trump, quite a position to maintain given he couldn’t voice his own audiobook and limited his press appearances for the release to a soft-focus People magazine story (his publisher did not respond to Party Animals’ multiple requests for an interview). According to the reviews, the former president dedicates scant attention to one of the biggest debacles of his presidency, the war in Gaza, which he abetted thanks to near-unwavering support for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as 2,000-pound bombs rained down on the densely packed enclave, killing more than 70,000 people.
