💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sci-fi fans would collectively agree that some stories of the genre are better off staying on the page.
  • Some of the greatest sci-fi books are written in a way that it is easy to directly adapt them for the screen.
  • The books' massive time jumps, anti-cinematic action, and prioritization of ideas over character beats made it impossible to adapt for the screen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sci-fi fans would collectively agree that some stories of the genre are better off staying on the page. For long, it was also believed that Isaac Asimov's books could not be translated to the screen, and for good reason. Especially when it comes to the Foundation book series, it was hard not to believe it was largely "unfilmable.".

Some of the greatest sci-fi books are written in a way that it is easy to directly adapt them for the screen. Isaac Asimov's Foundation books, in contrast, defy almost every rule of visual drama. It unfolds less as a fictional drama and more as a deep dive into everything from sociological mechanics to human psychology. While at it, it also spans across centuries, shifting its focus from one character to another.

The books' massive time jumps, anti-cinematic action, and prioritization of ideas over character beats made it impossible to adapt for the screen. This explains why many planned big-budget adaptations of the books also struggled to see the light of day in the past. Fortunately, however, Apple TV's Foundation took a massive risk and achieved the impossible by successfully adapting Isaac Asimov's books.

Impossible feats demand extreme risks. Owing to this, Apple TV's take on the Foundation books significantly changed the source material's approach. The biggest adaptation challenge came from the books' revolving characters. Every few chapters, the books experience time jumps, where old characters die of age and fresh ones emerge.

On the screen, viewers need rootable visual anchors who appear for longer periods.

Apple TV's Foundation carefully navigated this matter by introducing cloning, cyro-sleep, and digital consciousness. These became narrative devices that allowed the series to logically sustain the same characters and cast members across centuries and seasons. Even an immortal humanoid, named Lady Demerzel, emerges in Foundation from Asimov's wider universe.

It has been revealed that unlike the books, Apple TV's Foundation also visualizes key conflicts and collapses from the original story instead of solely focusing on their political implications. Even "psychohistory" from Isaac Asimov's Foundation gets a visual and more tangible representation in the series.

According to recent reports, armed with the Socratic method, Apple TV's Foundation understands that "The beginning of wisdom is the definition of terms." Instead of treating Asimov's story as a plot to be faithfully transcribed, the show first understands the true essence of its terms. It then turns into a more sprawling space-opera by wisely redefining its ideas.

Many readers have complained that Apple TV's Foundation is too distinct compared to its source material. They argue that it is unfair to even call it a worthy adaptation. It is hard not to agree with them. An adaptation cannot be considered great if it is a far cry from its source material.

Similar to Stanley Kubrick’s The Shining and Denis Villeneuve's Arrival, Foundation fails as a book-to-screen adaptation on many levels.

However, if purely judged as a modern television space opera, Foundation is easily one of the best sci-fi indicates of our time. While Asimov's books seemingly argue that historical forces matter far more than individual stories of heroism, Apple TV's Foundation carefully bends the original narrative to focus on almost mythic heroes and solo characters.

Sources indicate that it is also arguable that a direct page-to-page TV adaptation of Isaac Asimov's Foundation books would likely have failed. Whether Apple TV's adaptation approach is ideal is still debatable, but it at least gives us an epic sci-fi space opera.

According to recent reports, isaac Asimov's novel series is brought to life in Foundation, a television adaptation of the epic sci-fi saga created for Apple TV+. The show follows a group of exiled humans that find themselves as the last chance to save the Galactic Empire, primarily from itself.

Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1380 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • It has been revealed that install Python on your system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

It has been revealed that install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Sources indicate that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of new-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

On Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Users can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

Industry observers note that if you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Sources indicate that plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

It has been revealed that tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Sources indicate that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Recent findings suggest that force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

Recent findings suggest that mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

Sources indicate that my cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

According to recent reports, it's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

It has been revealed that your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

Sources indicate that most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. How to hide the newly introduced macOS 27.3 menu bar indicator

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (325 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override.
  • If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar.
  • I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds a blue menu bar indicator for apps using System & App Protection Override. Apple describes itas a transparency indicator that appears when one app is controlling another.

If you regularly use trusted automation tools and utilities, that can mean a persistent pill taking up space in your menu bar. Prefer to hide it? There’s a Terminal workaround.

I’ve tested this on macOS 27.3 beta 2 and confirmed that the indicator disappears after a restart.

Open Terminal and run these two commands:.

sudo mkdir -p /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domainsudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR -dict Enabled -bool false.

Enter your Mac administrator password when prompted, then restart your Mac.

The command disables the internal AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR feature flag. It doesn’t remove apps from your permissions list, although you’ll no longer see this activity indicator.

To restore Apple’s default behavior, run:.

sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/FeatureFlags/Domain/TCC AX_TRANSPARENCY_INDICATOR.

Restart your Mac again to apply the reversal. This removes only the indicator override, preserving any other flags you may have configured.

This is an undocumented workaround tested on the current beta, so Apple could change or remove it in a future upgrade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched music streamers from Apple Music to Tidal. I like Tidal's strict anti-AI features, the fact that it pays higher royalties to artists than other major streamers, and its focus on high quality audio. I wrote a post featuring eight hacks for Tidal customers, but I wanted to highlight one in particular: How to transfer playlists without paying anything.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

In a recent development, install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

In a recent development, download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

According to recent reports, run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Mike Flanagan has built his career on adapting King's work, including his adaptation of Carrie and a planned television series for The Dark Tower.Last year,The Long Walk andThe Running Man hit theaters. However,one of King's most underrated adaptations is set to leave Netflix in less than a month.

In a recent development, that series is Castle Rock. Originally airing on Hulu, Castle Rock is unique because it isn't based on a single King book or short story. Instead, it's set in the fictional town of Castle Rock, where most of King's stories take place. Despite its seemingly original story, Castle Rock pulls characters from King's work into a swirling web of murder, mystery, and magic. Horror fans will have to move quickly, as Castle Rock ​​​​​​departs Netflix on December 14. They won't want to miss it, because this series does something upcoming with King's work rather than being a straight adaptation.

Industry observers note that from the jump, Castle Rock isn't shy about showcasing characters and locations from Stephen King's work. Season 1's central mystery lies within Shawshank State Penitentiary, the titular prison in The Shawshank Redemption. Aspiring writer Jackie Torrance.

Sources indicate that (Jane Levy) is the niece of The Shining's protagonist, Jack Torrance, and Season 2 takes things a step further by introducing Lizzy Caplan as Annie Wilkes, who becomes the main villain in Misery. Co-showrunner Sam Shaw would later explain that he and Dustin Thomason wanted each season of Castle Rock to feel like its own separate story.

"The blueprint for the show, in the beginning, was to tell a different kind of original Stephen King story every season. This season is a ten hour story with a beginning, a middle, and an end, and we hope we will have a satisfying conclusion to all the trajectories that get introduced.".

According to recent reports, indeed, both seasons of Castle Rock feel like two distinct stories. Season 1 focuses on Henry Deaver (André Holland), who's drawn back to Castle Rock after a mysterious Shawshank prisoner referred to as "The Kid" (Bill Skarsgard) requests his presence. As Henry uncovers the Kid's origins, he deals with the shadows of his past, including the death of his adoptive father. Season 2 deals with Annie's descent into mass murder while incorporating elements from Salem's Lot. Though Castle Rock lasted only two seasons, it captured the feeling of a good Stephen King novel.

Industry observers note that fans who enjoy Castle Rock or are sad that it's leaving Netflix are in luck, as the streamer has another great King adaptation in the form of 11.22.63. Like Castle Rock, 11.22.63 originally debuted on Hulu and was produced under J.J. Abrams' Bad Robot banner. But while Castle Rock is merely inspired by Stephen King's work, 11.22.63 is a straight adaptation of one of his novels, in which teacher Jake Epping (James Franco) discovers a portalto 1963 in his friend's diner. Jake is tasked with stopping the assassination of John F. Kennedy, entering a literal race against time and a thriller that'll have viewers on the edge of their seats.

Industry observers note that one of Castle Rock's stars would reveal the plot for Season 3 last year, which would have hewed closer to one of King's novels than previous seasons. At Emerald City Comic Con in 2025, Jane Levy stated aims were in place for Castle Rock to center on Jackie Torrance, especially since Season 1 ends with her on a journey to learn more about her family. Castle Rock proves that Stephen King's work can inspire unique stories beyond adaptations, as its approach revealed a deep appreciation for allhis books.

Breaking: 90-Episode Legal Drama Mastered The Art Of Plot Twists

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although one ABC legal drama from the 2010s featured some of the wildest plot twists in TV history, the decline of this genre in the years that followed highlights a sad truth about TV’s future.
  • Perry Mason and Matlock were both early pioneers of the small-screen legal drama format, with Ally McBeal’s success reigniting interest in the genre in the ‘90s.
  • Industry observers note that the same year that Rhimes’s still underrated political drama Scandal started its seven-season run, the producer helped green light creator Peter Nowalk’s mystery/legal drama genre blender.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although one ABC legal drama from the 2010s featured some of the wildest plot twists in TV history, the decline of this genre in the years that followed highlights a sad truth about TV’s future. As far back as 1957’s 12 Angry Men, 1959’s Anatomy of a Murder, and 1962’s To Kill a Mockingbird, the legal thriller has been a staple of cinema. It was not long before TV caught up with this trend.

Perry Mason and Matlock were both early pioneers of the small-screen legal drama format, with Ally McBeal’s success reigniting interest in the genre in the ‘90s. As popular as these highlights were, it wasn’t until Grey’s Anatomy’s iconic producer Shonda Rhimes took to the genre in 2014 that the legal drama’s potential for shocking plot twists truly reached its full potential.

Industry observers note that the same year that Rhimes’s still underrated political drama Scandal started its seven-season run, the producer helped green light creator Peter Nowalk’s mystery/legal drama genre blender. Running for 90 episodes across six seasons on ABC, How To Get Away with Murder followed Viola Davis’s law professor Annalise Keating. Also working as a practicing defense attorney, Annalise found herself caught up in the investigations of not one, but two related murders in season 1 of the series.

What followed was a soapy, campy thrill ride that took the courtroom dramatics of reveals like The Lincoln Lawyer and fused it with the twisty, explosive plotting of Scandal. While How To Get Away with Murder’s competitors, such as The Good Wife and Suits, opted to focus mainly on the personal lives of their lawyer protagonists and the cases they took on separately, the ABC show blended these together.

Industry observers note that how To Get Away with Murder’s first audacious move was the decision to plant Annalise herself in the center of a murder investigation, then add another murder into the mix in short order. This set a high bar for the ABC series, as How To Get Away with Murder needed to provide steadily wider plot twists to keep viewers invested after this shocking start. Fortunately, the series was up to this task.

It is no exaggeration to say that How To Get Away with Murder perfected the art of the plot twist, starting out with a tone that was already somewhat larger than life and growing steadily sillier as the show continued. This might sound like a condemnation, but the delicate tonal balance required to gradually shift a show’s vibe is surprisingly tough to get right.

A lot of crime dramas and legal thrillers, like Netflix’s chilling Adolescence or the tragic true drama dramatization When They See Us, start serious and stay that way. Some, like Ryan Murphy’s instantly infamous All’s Fair, aim for an arch, playful tone, but end up feeling like they have no stakes thanks to their absurdity. Within this framework, the artful nature of How To Get Away with Murder’s twists becomes more apparent.

How To Get Away with Murder pulled off an impressive sleight of hand by starting out only slightly silly and over-the-top, as this left the show feeling glamorous but grounded. This ensured that How To Get Away with Murder’s increasingly shocking and silly plot twists never felt like a massive betrayal of the show’s original tone, unlike the many shows that start out much more realistic and end up far sillier.

It has been revealed that since teen indicates like Riverdale and the seven-season ABC mystery Pretty Little Liars began as believable small-town stories, their later seasons felt cartoonishly bizarre and detached from reality. However, How To Get Away with Murder’s earliest episodes were already just about heightened enough to justify the show’s later excesses, making even its wildest twists feel grounded within the show’s reality.

Eight Crucial Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (717 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet.
  • Recent findings suggest that your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network.
  • Recent findings suggest that some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand new or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Recent findings suggest that your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

Recent findings suggest that some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

According to recent reports, while some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

Industry observers note that your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

In a recent development, the password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

According to recent reports, two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets people connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Recent findings suggest that any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

In a recent development, routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO shook up the AI market and US economy last week, but now via The Wall Street Journal Huang has spoken out publicly for the first time since stepping down, and he signals he’s ready to return as CEO if asked.

Today Robbie Whelan at The Wall Street Journal published Jensen Huang’s first public statement since departing Nvidia last week.

It has been revealed that “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang stated in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the tech giant, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

To be clear, I’m also willing to step in as CEO of Nvidia if asked. I’ve owned several generations of their graphics cards, so I have plenty of experience with their products. More importantly, this is probably my best chance of finally having enough cash to afford a Mac with 32GB of RAM.

The timing is likely no coincidence, as Nvidia is set to report its quarterly earnings later today.

Sources indicate that even though Huang technically resigned as CEO rather than being fired, it was clear that his ouster wasn’t exactly his choice. Thus, today’s statement is the former CEO formally putting it out into the world that he’s ready to return if asked.

Since Huang stepped down, President Trump publicly called on Apple’s Tim Cook to step in as Nvidia CEO. But it’s expected that a fresh CEO—assuming it’s not Huang—will take much longer for the tech giant to find and Cook is unlikely to want the job.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Apple is currently beta testing the third major patch in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is currently beta testing the third major patch in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other latest features. But for owners of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This upgrade just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

In a recent development, now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software revision can introduce new hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

According to recent reports, apple made a significant deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That said, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some users may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the fresh option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are action stars, and then there is Jason Statham. There is no question that everyone has seen at least one of this performer's flicks, whether they know it or not. The English actor got his start as a Guy Ritchie favorite in movies such as Lock, Stock, and Two Smoking Barrels as well as Snatch. It was his entry into the classic Fast and the Furious franchise, however, that was not his most memorable role.

In a recent development, his part as the villain turned antihero contributed to him being an action star, but it still doesn’t compare to the action thriller to compare all action thrillers to. While it may not spring to mind with the greats such as The Transporter, Crank, or even the more recent Beekeeper, his magnum opus does what these other films only dream of.

At a certain point, Jason Statham has got to be in on the joke. The action star has been in too many different vocation-adjacent roles. It has become admirable how many times his characters can take another job where gunfights are necessary. The 2018 movie, The Meg, doesn’t quite fit into this category but also seems to be in on what Statham is selling. The Meg, of course, stands for megalodon, a prehistoric shark that is the focal point of the movie.

This is the type of narrative that is meant to be seen in theaters, but even if it isn’t, it is still a wild ride. The outrageous concept of a submarine crew encountering an extinct shark is a movie begging to be watched. This isn’t a self-serious journey into the waves. The Meg understands what it is about and doesn’t apologize for it.

Sources indicate that statham stars as Jonas Taylor, a renowned diver who has become known for crying megalodon. No one quite believes that his last crew was chomped to pieces by a giant shark, ushering him into a state of drunken retirement in Thailand. Of course, as these things go, no one can let sleeping sharks lie. Years later, another crew takes a journey into the treacherous waters and discovers that, yes, there is indeed a megalodon beneath the waters.

Even the characters in The Meg acknowledge the predicament they’re in. No one in their right mind would believe that Jonas saw a prehistoric shark, but they are all proven wrong when another crew gets endangered by its chomping jaws. They call in the only man who has claimed to see one, Jonas, himself. The Meg and its sequel are a fun ride, made purposefully for its underwater antics. It is a return to movies like Deep Blue Sea and even Jaws, where the most terrifying thing that exists is the rule of nature.

In a recent development, statham chews the scenery as he is wont to do, and no one does it better. The ensemble made up of Cliff Curtis and Rainn Wilson brings together the humor that this sort of movie couldn't do without. The Meg doesn’t hold back on the visuals either. If people pay to see a significant shark, they're going to see a big shark. It seems that all other attempts by Statham in later years were just a pale imitation of one of his best action thrillers. The Meg is quite literally all killer, no filler, and a visual treat for the senses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the firm’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

Professional and amateur photographers just got a upcoming alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the firm’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the company’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing owners to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:.

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

According to recent reports, the first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

According to recent reports, as for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Owners can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the company’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for swiftly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

And speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are new organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Recent findings suggest that once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, consumers can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

VSCO Studio Pro Desktop is available today as a free download for Apple Silicon Macs, with full feature access requiring a VSCO Pro membership, starting at $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year, or a VSCO One membership. You can see it in action below:.

#4136. Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1170 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Indiewire ↗ Open Full Page

Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1170 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not.
  • “It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger.

Recent findings suggest that “Wildwood” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. There isn’t the same kind of immersiveness for actors that live-action sets, costumes, and the basic pleasure of getting to read lines against other actors all provide. They have to build it from scratch. Related Stories Watch the ‘Backrooms’ VFX Supervisor Explain His Unique Process of Collaborating with Kane Parsons Aaron Pierre on ‘Lanterns,’ the DC Shake-Up, and Landing a Role in Ryan Gosling’s ‘Star Wars’ Movie.

“It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “So when you cast these things, it’s really interesting because sometimes the things we love about actors are not their voice; it’s everything else. So we will always listen, we’ll take clips from actors’ other films and their interviews, and we’ll put them against a design of a character.”.

Hearing a voice against a design can be revelatory, Knight believes, because it can teach a director and an animation team about who a character really is, whether a performer is really going to work or not, even before they step into the booth. It’s also an crucial way to help sort the whole of an ensemble so that actors occupy different aural frequencies and accents, and don’t sound too similar. You want to really be able to feel the difference between Carey Mulligan’s powerfully sinister Alexandra and Angela Bassett’s regal General.

And then, once the voice cast is in the booth, it’s also on the director and the team to help each voice actor sketch out all the different permutations of emotion the animators will then use as inspiration, and as tools.

“You’ll get the scene 30, 40, 50 different ways,” Knight said. “It takes forever. But, in the end, if you can do it properly, it feels like these characters are living in the same scene at the same time. And then it comes down to the animator to try to figure out how they can match the beauty of the vocal performance with the physical performance.”.

Recent findings suggest that that’s the normal process for feature animation: finding compelling voices, matching them with a design that feels spiritually connected to that voice, covering the performance many different ways, and then assembling a template for animators to build off of. And it’s the director, really, who has to hold in their head the many ways that the disparate parts will all come together.

According to recent reports, “An animator is an actor, but they’re just acting through their hands and through a puppet, and it’s two actors collaborating to create a complete performance. But oftentimes it happens across space, across time. And when it comes together in a harmonious way, it’s really beautiful because this thing seems like it’s completely alive,” Knight said.

But sometimes, voice actors’ performances do get to be alive together. That was a key creative choice that director Leah Nelson made for “Tangles” — it’s hard to argue with the logic of putting Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, and Bryan Cranston all in a room together to act out an earnest family drama, even if there’s a bit of mic bleed.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m so glad we [put them together]. And it wasn’t that hard. It took a little bit of scheduling Tetris to get it done, but it was so worthwhile,” Nelson told IndieWire. “Abbi does a ton of voice work, and often they’re alone and not even able to have someone to read against them. Sometimes they’re just doing the lines and sort of jumping around. And what I ultimately wanted was to have this really naturalistic dialogue.”.

In a recent development, “Tangles” boasts naturalism when it comes to sound, from bespoke foley to overlapping banter that isn’t meant to be precisely understood but to convey the chaos of one’s own (infuriating, loving) family. So Nelson and her team embraced the ways actors can build on each other, and even on improv, in recording the dialogue.

According to recent reports, “A lot of humor came out of giving them time to not only play with the dialogue but to play with each other. But also, those really intimate and difficult moments of the film, they could look in each other’s eyes and work through those moments. That was crucial to me, and it was important to them as well. So it was an experience we all went through together.”.

It has been revealed that the one downside of treating recording sessions more like the rehearsals for a play is the risk of wrecking takes. “We spent a lot of time at the table trying to hold [our reactions] in or like, ‘Don’t sneeze! Nobody move!’” Nelson joked. “But I didn’t want it to sound like there was so much suturing; the mastery of the dialogue editing to make it all sound naturalistic, so we also did a lot of work to make that happen. But what we had to work with felt very naturalistic to begin with.”.

The ultimate example of naturalistic voice acting, however, might be on display in “Wildwood.” Knight’s own son was a newborn while the team was laying down track for the film, which made him the perfect actor for the role of kidnapped Baby Mac.

Recent findings suggest that “I essentially chased him around the house with a digital recorder. Sometimes with my iPhone. I was just trying to coax things out of him, make him laugh and giggle and verbalize. And the thing about babies is that they’re constantly trying to make sense of the world,” Knight said. “They’re always babbling and trying to make shapes with their mouths. So we have a lot of that babbling in the movie, and it helped make it feel naturalistic.”.

It speaks to the wide-ranging power of voice acting in animation: you can get to naturalism through a grounded collaboration between actors, an actor in complete isolation, or hitting “record” on an iPhone while you’re changing a diaper.

“Wildwood” is now in theaters. “Tangles” releases in theaters on January 15, 2027.

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.”.

Powered by the new Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1286 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth.
  • The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.
  • Industry observers note that an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

Industry observers note that an isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

Industry observers note that one of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Industry observers note that is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

Industry observers note that if you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it significant and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for newly introduced planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

It has been revealed that if you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous newly introduced reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

Industry observers note that if you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend indicates a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bill Hader‘s first film as a director has found its distribution partner. Black Bear has acquired North American distribution rights to “They Know,” Hader’s upcoming psychological horror film that he co-stars in with Linda Cardellini. The growing distributor, which just released “Wicker” nationwide, acquired the rights from financier MRC in what was described as a competitive situation.

Per an official synopsis, “They Know” follows a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wife’s newly introduced mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children.

In a recent development, “Bill Hader is a singular talent both in front of and behind the camera, and he has delivered a film in ‘They Know’ unlike anything we’ve ever seen,” Black Bear president of production & operations Michael Heimler said in a statement. “’They Know’ is authentic, original, and bold filmmaking at the highest level, and we couldn’t be more excited to partner with Bill and re-team with our great friends at MRC, who consistently deliver boundary-pushing films that help define their genre.” Related Stories Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation Watch the ‘Backrooms’ VFX Supervisor Explain His Unique Process of Collaborating with Kane Parsons.

Hader co-wrote “They Know” with Duffy Boudreau and produced alongside Bob Graf, with Alyssa Donovan co-producing.

Hader is a three-time Primetime Emmy winner for his work on “South Park” and “Barry.” He co-created the HBO comedy “Barry” with Alec Berg and began directing episodes in Season 2, gradually working his way up to directing the entirety of Season 4. He has long been open about his cinematic influences and his desire to transition into feature filmmaking after the show ended.

Recent findings suggest that hader recently shared some more details about directing his first feature while speaking at IndieWire’s Los Angeles Future of Filmmaking Summit. He explained that “They Know” emerged after he and longtime friend and writing partner Boudreau both went through divorces and discussed their biggest fears about ways the process could have gone awry.

“We’re both divorced. We were talking about how lucky we were that we were on, like, we had really good terms with our ex-wives, and we have kids with them,” Hader mentioned. “We started talking about the worst case scenarios of, ‘Oh, my god, this person is going through this and this person is going through that.’ And then this idea came up.”.

Black Bear has yet to announce a release date for “They Know.”.

Robert Pattinson’s Crime Thriller Is Still His Greatest Movie 9 Years Later

  • Sources indicate that with the recent announcement of his casting as James Bond, it's clear that Robert Pattinson has had a pretty good few years.
  • It has been revealed that released in 2017, Good Time, directed by Josh and Benny Safdie, is a relentless, anxiety-inducing thriller that centers on a small-time criminal who, after a failed robbery, attempts to rescue his brother.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Conor Sheeran is a Movies and TV features writer for Collider. He has a deep passion for cinema and watches everything from the biggest blockbusters to the smallest indies. While he specializes in movies and television, he has also written about politics, culture, and sports throughout his career. Based in Newly introduced York City, Conor is also a massive fan of the New York Jets, Mets, and Knicks. He is still waiting for any of those teams to bring home a championship in his lifetime. A member of the National Writers Union and the International Federation of Journalists, Conor is a strong proponent of press freedom and collective action.

Sources indicate that with the recent announcement of his casting as James Bond, it's clear that Robert Pattinson has had a pretty good few years. Since 2020, he's portrayed Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves' The Batman; appeared in two Christopher Nolan films, The Odyssey and Tenet; and garnered massive critical praise for performances in movies like The Drama, Primetime, and Mickey 17. While he had once been known mainly for his starring role in the Twilight franchise, he has emerged as one of Hollywood's best actors. But even amid this run of incredible performances, his greatest role remains the one that arrived nearly a decade ago.

It has been revealed that released in 2017, Good Time, directed by Josh and Benny Safdie, is a relentless, anxiety-inducing thriller that centers on a small-time criminal who, after a failed robbery, attempts to rescue his brother. Set in a grimy and disturbingly unromantic New York City, Good Time is a nightmarish descent into the criminal underworld, a landscape where desperation, violence, and self-destruction are commonplace. Though Pattinson has become even more well-known for his turns in some of Hollywood's biggest films, his performance in Good Time was his finest role, and one that has yet to be beaten in his filmography.

Sources indicate that on the surface, the premise of Good Time is straightforward and has few complications. Pattinson's Connie Nikas, along with his intellectually disabled brother Nick (Bennie Safdie), attempts to rob a bank. The heist goes wrong almost from the start, and when Nick is arrested and sent to jail, Connie pulls out all the stops to get the money together to bail him out, regardless of the consequences.

According to recent reports, much like one of the Safdies' other films, Uncut Gems, Good Time is relentless in its tension, drama, and thrills that have you on the verge of a heart attack throughout. Connie's journey through Newly introduced York City on his desperate quest to free his brother is equal parts frustrating and devastating. Every decision he makes as he traverses the city only seems to make his situation worse, pulling him into more dangerous problems with hardened criminals and complete strangers.

Recent findings suggest that the film unfolds with the momentum of a 100-minute panic attack, never letting you catch your breath or process what you just watched before it jumps into the next disastrous development. Its close-up shooting style and claustrophobic framing pull you right into the drama and feel genuinely suffocating. There is something uniquely exhausting about watching Connie operate. Like the viewer, he never pauses to think about what is happening; he is always moving, talking, and searching for a way out. However, much like a man trapped in quicksand, the quicker he moves, the deeper he sinks into the consequences of his actions.

What truly elevates the movie beyond its already exceptional filmmaking is Pattinson's performance. For a long time, Pattinson was brushed off as "the Twilight guy," but it was films like Good Time that helped him shake off that perception and show general audiences his true, vast range. Connie is hardly a likable protagonist and is anything but conventional, much less a person anyone should admire. For all the love he has for Nick, Connie is selfish, manipulative, and cruel, someone who is willing to exploit nearly everyone he comes across to accomplish what he's set out to do.

Pattinson's performance is built around this fascinating dichotomy: a personality that makes little sense, yet you can tell he genuinely loves his brother. He's resourceful yet incompetent, someone who is selfish and selfless while using what street smarts he has to escape danger without considering larger consequences.

In a recent development, the actor captures these contradictions with impressive skill, a test that many other actors would fail. His frantic physicality, aggression, and ability to shift from charm to intimidation at a moment's notice make him feel like a real human and not a caricature. At times, it's almost easy to forget you're watching "that guy from Twilight" as Pattinson disappears into this character with his bleached hair and disheveled appearance. He is so far removed from a polished romantic lead that you start to question whether it's truly the same performer.

In a recent development, since the premiere of Good Time, Pattinson has become even bigger than he was at the height of the Twilight era. He is set to play James Bond, he's Batman, and he is a frequent potential nominee for numerous Academy Awards. For all the good he does now, it was films like Good Time that first showed audiences what he was made of.

According to recent reports, nearly a decade after its release, the movie remains an extraordinary achievement, not just because of its incredible direction, narrative, and cinematography, but because Pattinson delivers a performance that continues to define his abilities. He may have become James Bond, but Connie Nikas remains his most unforgettable creation.

Good Time is streaming free on the Roku Channel.

  • Unlike Midnight X-Men, which has roots in an incredibly familiar history of Marvel Comics X-Men lore, Midnight Spider-Man is wholly unique.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlike Midnight X-Men, which has roots in an incredibly familiar history of Marvel Comics X-Men lore, Midnight Spider-Man is wholly unique. It begins with Peter Parker’s brand-fresh origin story, which shares core principles of the character’s traditional depiction but ultimately disfigures it into something far more tragic and nightmarish (complementarily, as this is a horror story, after all, not a superhero story).

Sources indicate that concern #1 was essentially Midnight Spider-Man’s “Amazing Fantasy #15” in this regard, and issue #2 followed its startling cliffhanger fairly closely by briefly illustrating a couple of Spider-Man’s newfound superpowers: spider-sense, or at least some ultra instinct variant of it depicted by red flares, and super-strength, which he demonstrated when he got hold of Oscorp security officers Gargan and Rodriguez. If the last few pages of issue #2 are any indication, it’s incredibly likely that Felicia Hardy will gain powers of her own soon.

Sources indicate that midnight Spider-Man’s Felicia Hardy is surprisingly something of a deuteragonist in the narrative, and that’s been heavily reinforced by how strong a presence she has in the book’s myriad covers, whether they’re main covers or variants. It’s been difficult to discern what role she would have in the story based on these covers alone, especially with some newly revealed covers now implying that she and a freshly 18-year-old Peter will have some sort of romantic or sexual relationship. If that’s true, it may not be for a little while, as Felicia was quite terrified when she found him in the terrifying state he was in.

When she is tasked to retrieve the spider, which Octavius believes would be dead after absorbing all the radiation and pharmaceuticals it did, Felicia is stunned to see that it has latched onto Peter and grotesquely mutated him. It’s unknown how much control Peter actually has over himself here, but he recognizes Felicia and pleads with her to help him. At the end of the issue, he rushes past her and jumps out a window without harming her.

However, at the end of Midnight Spider-Man #2, Felicia notices a wound on her arm, possibly inadvertently inflicted by Peter. If so, the book probably wouldn’t have made a note of it, much less leave this cut as its cliffhanger for the second issue, if it wasn’t going to have a massive effect on her character, and that could manifest by way of superpowers.

In a recent development, midnight Spider-Man #2 reveals a much more sympathetic shade of this Felicia, who seemed like a villainous predator—she’s Oscorp’s vice president of talent relations, after all, and Oscorp is a hellish antagonist in Marvel’s Midnight continuity. She had clearly never met with Oscorp’s Dr. Otto Octavius before, and, even if she isn’t surprised or mortified by the gory research he and his assistants conduct, an effort is made to portray her as an underling who might question her allegiances now that things have truly gotten out of hand.

It has been revealed that peter slicing Felicia’s arm and accidentally giving her monstrous abilities would align perfectly with the book’s apparent dedication to tormenting this iteration of Spider-Man. He may not have split her head apart, but afflicting her with a mutation comparable to his might be a fate worse than death.

The only snag in this logic is that it would be a rather odd way for Felicia to obtain powers because it would give her spider-related powers, if anything. Of course, we know little about Felicia as a character as is in this universe, and she may never become a version of the Black Cat antihero she is in traditional Marvel Comics lore.

According to recent reports, that said, the solicitation for Midnight Spider-Man #5 reveals that “the mutation that created Spider-Man has spread to a new host... with shocking results,” and the chances of this host being Felicia have now skyrocketed. Otherwise, it could tease that the spider on Peter’s chest will make like a symbiote and bond with someone else. Either way, this solicit reads as follows:.

Oscorp’s second generation monstrosity is loose, and its first prey is Spider-Man. Meanwhile, the mutation that created Spider-Man has spread to a fresh host... with shocking results.

Midnight Spider-Man #2 is out now.

Google Wallet is now available on iOS to “organize purchases, tickets, boarding passes, and more in one easy place” in the US.

The Google Wallet app on iPhone does not offer tap-to-pay functionality due to platform restrictions. Instead, Google touts three intended use cases:.

App navigation is handled by a floating pill (in Liquid Glass) with two tabs. The homepage starts with a carousel of recent purchases slated for delivery, followed by boarding passes, and finally a grid of loyalty cards.

The next tab indicates a list of recent transactions associated with Google. The Wallet app will display purchase emails and summarize them. You also get a list of Passes, which you can pin/unpin from the homepage, and payment methods saved to your Google Account.

Sources indicate that the ‘plus’ FAB (floating action button) lets you add loyalty, gift, and payment cards (for use in Chrome). There’s a convenient “Everything else” camera scanner that can be used to digitize anything else.

The other main reason Google Wallet now exists on iOS is that the organization wants the app to be a “secure hub for managing agentic purchases across Google.”.

Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects.

Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra can use that screenshot as a template and match the layout, colors, and even the font size.

On the Codex side, OpenAI states Astra is better at making and testing changes in an existing project.

“Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision,” OpenAI states.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

With both models at maximum reasoning effort, OpenAI claims Sol came within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost.

The $200/month Pro initiative also gets Ultrafast mode for the first time with Sol. The $500/month Pro plan gets Ultrafast on both models, as do eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces once an admin enables it.

According to recent reports, how fast is Ultrafast? OpenAI notes it can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate on either model, although it uses more of your allowance. You can switch speeds from the model picker.

It has been revealed that developers can use both models through the API today as well. Astra’s standard input and output prices are 20% lower than with GPT-6 Astra, while Sol keeps its GPT-6.1 pricing.

Light is one of the biggest triggers for your body clock. A lack of light signals it's time to sleep, while bright lights help you feel alert. It's a reason why many of us (including me) find it easier to wake up in summer, when the sun has naturally risen by the time you're getting out of bed.

In winter, however, dark mornings often lead to sleep inertia. Instead of being slowly woken by the rising sun, you're jolted awake by an alarm screeching in the middle of your sleep cycle.
