Before Firefly, A 110-Episode Sci-Fi Masterpiece Changed Space Operas Forever

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, some sci-fi shows do not need multiple seasons to leave lasting legacies.
  • Many great sci-fi shows have landed on streaming in the last two decades, with quite a few of them being compelling space operas.
  • Firefly's full potential remains unfulfilled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some sci-fi shows do not need multiple seasons to leave lasting legacies. In just one season and as few as 14 episodes, they manage to create ripples through television's past, present, and future. Fox's Firefly is one such rare sci-fi space opera that was unfortunately canceled after just one season. In the years that followed, though, it became a viral cult phenomenon with an undying legacy.

Many great sci-fi shows have landed on streaming in the last two decades, with quite a few of them being compelling space operas. Yet, many cannot help but rewatch and remember Firefly's Western and space fusion, found family theme, and relatable blue-collar worldbuilding. Long before Firefly, however, another space opera, Babylon 5, completely changed the genre forever.

Firefly's full potential remains unfulfilled. Who knows, the show could have had an even bigger following and a stronger legacy if it had been given the chance to realize its complete story. Fortunately, for Babylon 5, it got to reach its natural conclusion despite facing the threat of cancelation after season 4. Even before Babylon 5 ended its run, though, it was already unlike any other sci-fi show of its time.

Recent findings suggest that some of the best sci-fi reveals in the '90s were written week-to-week. They had no definitive ending and each fresh episode served a story reset that allowed new viewers to tune in. Instead of following the crowd, J. Michael Straczynski (JMS) decided to create his own unique playbook for television. He wrote a television novel that came to be known as Babylon 5.

Industry observers note that even in the streaming era, where most shows are serialized and have some continuity across seasons, not every story arc is pre-planned. However, for Babylon 5, JMS planned a five-year arc even before the show began filming. Owing to this, even seemingly irrelevant throwaway lines and dream sequences from the show's opening season got worthy payoffs much later.

Sources indicate that babylon 5 also did not shy away from centering on morally flawed protagonists. Some of Babylon 5's best characters, like Londo Mollari and G'Kar, go through transformations throughout the show's runtime after their suffering either brings out the best or the worst in them.

Even from a scientific and political standpoint, Babylon 5 was surprisingly grounded in realism. Its portrayal of space travel relied heavily on Newtonian physics and centrifugal antigravity. Meanwhile, its political drama, too, was shaped around 20th century concerns like erosion of democracies and the impact of imperialism.

Firefly truly thrives when it focuses on the dynamics of its main misfit characters. Some of its greatest moments revolve around the quick, overlapping banter between Serenity's crew. This is why Firefly is remembered less as a grand space opera and more as an intimate portrayal of a found family's day-to-day survival in space.

In the long run, Firefly might have expanded its vision, but its short runtime primarily kept its story confined to its human relationships.

Babylon 5, on the other hand, heads more into the grand fantasy territory, reminiscent of the scale of storytelling in Tolkien and Isaac Asimov's stories. With its long 5-season runtime, it explores how civilizations rise, fall and collide while constantly moving outwards into geopolitical disaster. Even the characters in Babylon 5 transform to a point where they are almost unrecognizable towards the end.

It has been revealed that the threat of cancellation slightly ruined Babylon 5's forward momentum towards the end. However, like Firefly, the sci-fi series ensured that its legacy as an iconic space opera remains unscathed.

According to recent reports, babylon 5 is a science fiction television series set on a space station built by the Earth Alliance. Released in 1994, it acts as a diplomatic sanctuary to preserve peace among various alien races, doubling as a military post and a bustling hub for travelers and traders. As Commander Jeffrey Sinclair and later Captain John Sheridan oversee the station, they become caught in a growing conspiracy and an ancient conflict that threatens the future of the galaxy.

#4120. The 10 Most Inspired Oscar Wins of All Time, Ranked

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2232 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

The 10 Most Inspired Oscar Wins of All Time, Ranked

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2232 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every young person with a dream for Hollywood has certainly pretended what it might feel like to win an Academy Award.
  • From groundbreaking firsts to sweeps that reshaped the landscape of the awards and movies at large, these ten inspiring wins have stayed with us long beyond their speeches.
  • The history and legacy of songs in films leave a very different impression than the movies they came from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every young person with a dream for Hollywood has certainly pretended what it might feel like to win an Academy Award. They’ve held a hairbrush as a microphone, a shampoo bottle in hand, practicing their speech in front of the bathroom mirror. Many of those speeches come from those they have watched win on their TV. Whether it was an expected win or a massive shock, many inspiring victories have shaped generations that followed. We’re here to celebrate ten.

From groundbreaking firsts to sweeps that reshaped the landscape of the awards and movies at large, these ten inspiring wins have stayed with us long beyond their speeches. While many other groundbreaking Academy Award wins changed Hollywood, these ten represent a well-rounded mix of categories, eras, and legacies. Whose Oscar win made the greatest impact on you?

The history and legacy of songs in films leave a very different impression than the movies they came from. Not only can we enjoy them on their own, but they also bring us back to that moment when we heard them on the silver screen. For a long time, the Best Original Song winners maintained a specific essence and style. Then the 21st Century came and the times had changed. Once Eminem won for “Lose Yourself,” the door was open for Three 6 Mafia to win for “It’s Hard Out Here for a Pimp.” Winning for the film Hustle & Flow, the song emerged victorious as it captured the grit, struggle, and ambition of the film's main character, DJay (Terrence Howard), in a way that resonated emotionally.

According to recent reports, the hip-hop group’s victory didn’t come as a shock for defeating Dolly Parton, but because of how it proved that independent, underground Southern hip-hop artists could reach mainstream Hollywood success without compromising their roots. Coming out of Memphis, Three 6 Mafia was an unlikely contender in a traditional award show setting, making their victory feel like a win for "outsiders.” They became the first hip-hop group to win an Academy Award and perform at the ceremony, making the night’s milestone even sweeter. Members Juicy J and DJ Paul didn't expect to win and had no prepared acceptance speech, but their enthusiasm reverberated through the room.

Recent findings suggest that if there’s one thing that Bob Fosse is, it’s specific. Though he had been in the director’s seat in the past, his greatest cinematic triumph came through in his semi-autobiographical film All That Jazz. The legendary choreographer had a vision, and editor Alan Heim delivered. Though the Oscar went solely to Heim, Fosse collaborated quite closely with him in the cutting room. Heim and Fosse shaped the film with a driving, musical pace, blending theatrical choreography, rehearsal footage, and surreal sequences into a cohesive pulse. As Roy Scheider’s Joe Gideon nears physical collapse, the editing shifts fluidly between gritty backstage reality, hospital scenes, and elaborate musical fantasies.

It has been revealed that building on techniques discovered while editing Lenny, Heim moved fluidly across timelines and wove fantasy and dream logic into a straight narrative. This mirrors a mind under intense physical and creative strain. Techniques like cutting slightly off the beat or overlapping dialogue keep momentum high without feeling mechanical. Heim described moving time around and collaborating with Fosse as a creative adventure. Heim’s victory was a creative win. His win came against tough competition, beating heavy hitters including Apocalypse Now and Kramer vs. Kramer. The wildcard win highlighted how complex, long-gestating post-production can reward visual and rhythmic craftsmanship. Heim’s artistry is a benchmark of ambitious editing.

Industry observers note that sometimes playing yourself, or at least a version of it, can lead to massive success. For Diane Keaton, playing Annie Hall came as old hat, as Woody Allen modeled the titular character around her, name and all. Incorporating her natural mannerisms, humor, and tomboyish style was all it took as the Academy voters praised her fresh, self-deprecating comedic timing and nuanced portrayal of an awkward yet intelligent woman. Rather than playing a one-note "ditzy" character, Keaton balanced nervous tics and awkwardness with genuine intelligence and vulnerability. Her vintage menswear wardrobe of vests, ties, baggy trousers, and hats helped turn her into a defining late-1970s style icon.

Keaton’s victory for Annie Hall broke traditional conventions, celebrating individuality over traditional Hollywood glamour. Her candid, low-key acceptance moment stood out against overly scripted awards-show polish, making the win feel genuine and approachable. By redefining the leading lady through her achingly real presentation, Keaton influenced generations of performers and viewers alike. Sharp-witted, neurotic, and self-deprecating personas can be as equally charming as the formally polished presentation of a romantic damsel.

Before Get Out, most audiences knew Jordan Peele from his sketch comedy days. Then his directorial debut rattled cinema as a genuine Hollywood player. The film was a massive success, largely because of Peele’s groundbreaking original screenplay. Peele was awarded for writing an original horror-satire script that blended suspense with sharp social commentary on modern Black experiences. He combined psychological horror and satire into what he called a "social thriller," addressing themes underrepresented in mainstream horror cinema. Peele’s victory was monumental because he became the first Black writer to win the category. Only three other creators of color had been nominated in the category before him: Suzanne de Passé, Spike Lee, and John Singleton.

According to recent reports, shot in 23 days on a $4.5 million budget, Get Out proved that tight constraints and unconventional premises could yield major critical and commercial success. Peele framed the moment as part of a wider renaissance in Black filmmaking, encouraging young creators to claim their voices and tell stories that challenge industry norms. Peele shared in his acceptance speech that he stopped writing the script about 20 times because he doubted it would ever get made, yet kept returning to it because he believed people needed to hear and see the story. That part alone reminds anyone watching, no matter their craft, of the power of resilience. Coming from a low-budget debut by a writer-director best known for sketch comedy, Peele broke long-standing Oscar barriers for horror films and Black screenwriters. Underdogs rise up!​​​​​​​.

It has been revealed that when we examine the top-tier actors in cinema history, that list almost certainly includes Marlon Brando. His style of acting was on full display in On the Waterfront, and he was rewarded for it. He won the Academy Award because of his groundbreaking, naturalistic method-acting performance as dockworker Terry Malloy. His approach stood out as both intense and lifelike compared to traditional theatrical screen acting. The win marked Brando's fourth consecutive Best Actor nomination, signaling that Academy voters were ready to reward his sustained impact.

Recent findings suggest that brando’s performance paired working-class grit with quiet pain and moral awakening, most famously in the backseat cab scene in which he uttered, “I could have been a contender.” Brando was in quite a tough category, besting Humphrey Bogart, Bing Crosby, James Mason, and Dan O'Herlihy. Brando’s inspirational win validated emotional vulnerability beneath a tough exterior, influencing future elite actors including Daniel Day-Lewis and Joaquin Phoenix. Though Brando’s victory did not come as a shock, it was part of the film’s eight-award sweep that night. ​​​​​​​.

Sources indicate that stanley Kubrick’s imprint on cinema is quite profound. Though his career includes many monumental moments, his victory alongside John Alcott for Best Cinematography is the most inspiring. Winning for the film Barry Lyndon, the victory came from its groundbreaking low-light filming techniques and a painterly visual style that recreated an 18th-century world without electric light. Capturing enough light in near darkness, Alcott and Kubrick used ultra-fast Zeiss Planar 50mm f/0.7 lenses originally created for NASA low-light photography. Exterior scenes relied on natural daylight and careful light control rather than heavy artificial setups.

The victory inspired future filmmakers because it proved authentic, period-accurate visuals could be achieved through daring technical problem-solving rather than standard Hollywood shortcuts. Principal photography took roughly 300 days across multiple countries, highlighting a close working relationship between a demanding director and a cinematographer willing to go the distance to achieve greatness. The win wasn’t undeserved, but rather shocking due to the overall sentiment regarding the slower, 3-hour period piece. While it competed against stiff competition like Jaws and One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest in other categories, there was no denying the inspiring influence of artistic creativity and ingenuity on the film’s cinematography.​​​​​​​.

Firsts always have a massive impact, but Halle Berry’s monumental win for Best Actress was huge. For her role as Leticia Musgrove in Monster’s Ball, Berry was the first Black woman to win in that category. The win came to some as a shock, as the Golden Globes tend to be a predictor for the Oscars. She lost to Sissy Spacek for In the Bedroom. She won against a stacked lineup that included Dame Judi Dench for Iris, Nicole Kidman for Moulin Rouge!, Spacek for In the Bedroom, and Renée Zellweger for Bridget Jones's Diary.

Recent findings suggest that in her acceptance speech, she dedicated the moment to "every nameless, faceless woman of color" and honored trailblazers and peers who shaped her path. She took on a demanding, low-paying dramatic part despite warnings about its difficult and explicit material. The role itself drew intense discussion around portrayals of Black women and female sexuality, but even with her win, Hollywood's casting habits did not fundamentally shift overnight. That same ceremony saw Denzel Washington win Best Actor, marking the only time both top acting Oscars went to performers of color in the same year. ​​​​​​​.

Foreign language films rarely earned mainstream representation in the Best Picture category. When they do, it’s a formality and almost like a participation trophy. But then, one profound film walked away with the top honor: Parasite. Directed by Bong Joon Ho, the film earned the award because of its universal themes of class inequality, genre-blending craftsmanship, strong word-of-mouth among voters, and late-season awards momentum. It became the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture. Voters praised its tight structure, foreshadowing, ensemble acting, and seamless shifts between comedy, thriller, and drama.

Recent findings suggest that bong's win, echoing the idea that the most personal is the most creative, highlighted the power of distinct, auteur-driven storytelling. The win revealed that non-English films and international creators can reach the highest level of mainstream awards recognition rather than be confined to international categories. It broadened global representation and encouraged viewers to explore cinema beyond Hollywood. While Sam Mendes’ 1917 entered the season as the clear frontrunner, the director’s charismatic campaigning, strong backing, and enthusiastic recommendations from voters helped overcome the traditional subtitle barrier. Now we celebrate foreign-language films as genuine contenders each year. ​​​​​​​.

It has been revealed that sequels rarely get a chance for Oscar glory, let alone the third chapter of a franchise. Then The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King proved the naysayers completely wrong. Not only did the Peter Jackson adaptation have a good night at the 2004 Academy Awards, but it also swept all 11 of its Oscar nominations! Because The Fellowship of the Ring and The Two Towers had earned major nominations and technical wins without capturing Best Picture or Best Director, voters treated the finale as a cumulative reward for the entire trilogy, backed by a massive studio campaign that overcame longtime Academy bias against fantasy films. The Return of the King tied the all-time Oscar record held by Ben-Hur and Titanic.

Recent findings suggest that shooting an entire trilogy back-to-back over years was an unprecedented risk that reaped a beneficial reward. Winning celebrated a story rooted in courage, hope, friendship, and enduring human effort during a turbulent era. Fantasy had historically struggled to win top honors at the Oscars, making the clean sweep a watershed moment that helped break that barrier. What may come as a shock is that the massive achievement came even though none of the cast members received an acting nomination. ​​​​​​​.

Horror rarely received a seat at the table. Then The Silence of the Lambs not only received an invitation, it was the true guest of honor. The film earned the rare honor of winning the “Big Five”—Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Actress, and Best Adapted Screenplay. It became the third film in Oscar history to win all five major categories, joining It Happened One Night and One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest. Jonathan Demme's direction emphasized psychological tension and character empathy over constant gore, working from Ted Tally's adaptation of Thomas Harris' novel. Jodie Foster as FBI trainee Clarice Starling and Anthony Hopkins, with roughly 16 minutes of screen time, as Hannibal Lecter, anchored the story with intense, memorable acting.

Defying the odds, its dark themes, cannibalism, and graphic violence felt far removed from traditional prestige Oscar fare. The Silence of the Lambs proved a dark thriller film could earn top-tier prestige rather than being dismissed as mere genre entertainment. Another shocker in its victory was its time of release. Coming out in February 1991, it won 13 months later—showing a film that did not need a late-year release to stay in the Oscar conversation. Though it faced off against massive contenders like Beauty and the Beast and faced protests outside the ceremony over its portrayal of killer Jame Gumb, controversy and competition were nothing for the massive hit.

Why iPhone Duo wasn’t for me (but might be for you)

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it.
  • I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands.
  • Sources indicate that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve had the iPhone Duo for nearly two weeks now, and have officially decided to return it. Here are the three main reasons why the Duo didn’t work out for me, but might for you.

I use my iPhone one-handed all the time, and based on my experience, iPhone Duo is clearly intended to be used with two hands. You can use it one-handed, but for me it’s not nearly as comfortable as the iPhone 18 Pro. It’s too wide and too heavy to be used for long.

Sources indicate that perhaps over time I’d get used to needing two hands for most iPhone interactions. But that would be a pretty significant shift for me, as there are so many situations when I don’t have both hands free.

If you already use two hands with your iPhone regularly—perhaps because you have a Pro Max model—then the Duo’s one-handed experience likely won’t bother you. But the more I used the Duo, the more I found myself missing my iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest value proposition of a foldable is that it’s a 2-in-1 product, letting you have a standard phone but also a tablet-sized display that fits in your pocket.

According to recent reports, I totally get the appeal, and fully expected to love that hybrid design. But after two weeks of trying, I still struggled to find times when I actually wanted to unfold the Duo. And to be clear, that’s a me problem, not an problem with the Duo itself.

I tried a bunch of apps on the inner display, and struggled to find use cases that—for me—made it worthwhile to open the Duo. But based on the feedback I’ve seen from most Duo owners, I’m very much in the minority.

According to recent reports, I know lots of people love the Duo for video, but I don’t watch much video on my iPhone. I almost never watch YouTube, TikTok, or Instagram Reels. And for shows and movies, I stick with my TV screen and an Apple TV 4K.

It has been revealed that multitasking support on iPhone Duo works really well. But when I found myself needing to multitask, I still reached for my iPad Pro with Magic Keyboard attached. A keyboard-free product can’t replace my main computer (nor would I expect it to), and the Duo screen was too small to comfortably work on it.

Industry observers note that last year I bought an iPhone Air and absolutely loved it. Initially, the Air’s less capable camera system didn’t bother me, it was “good enough.”.

After a few months though, I started missing the Pro camera system more. Then I learned that my wife was pregnant with twins, and I knew I wanted the best possible iPhone cameras to capture their early weeks and months. So I bought an iPhone 18 Pro in September.

I’ve been very impressed by iPhone 18 Pro’s Main camera upgrades, and it’s great having a Telephoto lens again too. Since having the best camera system is so crucial for me right now, I knew iPhone Duo couldn’t be my only iPhone.

It has been revealed that I initially planned to dual-carry the two models, using iPhone 18 Pro solely as a camera. But over and over I found myself wishing it was my only iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that I returned mine as well. Beautiful device, but functionally not very good.

Sources indicate that is the iPhone Duo camera good enough for most people? Probably so. But for this year at least, with my twins aging rapidly, it’s not quite right for me. If I loved the Duo for other reasons, I would just use both models. But since I didn’t, I’m happy to stick with the iPhone 18 Pro.

In closing, I want to explicitly state that I don’t think the iPhone Duo is a bad product, and this isn’t a “bad review.”.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Duo just isn’t for me. I get the sense, though, that it’s lots of people’s favorite iPhone in years. Apple created its most unique new iPhone model since the original, and there’s plenty to love about it. I’m very curious to see how popular foldables become over time compared to slab models, because each clearly offers pros and cons. But for me, at least right now, the iPhone 18 Pro is my model of choice.

According to recent reports, what has your iPhone Duo experience been like so far? Love it? Undecided? Let us know in the comments.

Custom EQ is a feature that some AirPods people thought Apple would never ship, but iOS 27 adds it.

It has been revealed that with Custom EQ, Apple now lets you set your own sound profile for AirPods. Per Apple:.

In a recent development, airPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV highlights and movies, and calls. If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.

Apple GymKit has been available for years, but only for Apple Watch. It lets you pair and sync workout data with compatible cardio equipment, like treadmills, ellipticals, indoor bikes, and more.

In iOS 27, GymKit expands to support iPhone using AirPods Pro 3’s heart rate sensor. My colleague Zac gave it a try:.

In a recent development, the setup is simple. I tapped my iPhone to the treadmill, picked Indoor Walk (Indoor Run is also offered), and started the workout from the treadmill. With GymKit, workout data is stored privately on iPhone and removed from the equipment.

According to recent reports, once the workout started, the treadmill received heart-rate data from AirPods Pro 3. Meanwhile, the Fitness app on iPhone received the treadmill’s distance, pace, incline, and calorie data. Treadmills know details that an iPhone and AirPods can’t know on their own, especially incline and precise belt distance.

Industry observers note that earlier this year when AirTag 2 introduced, Apple brought Precision Finding support to Apple Watch for the first time. Until now though, it’s been limited to AirTag 2.

But with iOS 27 and watchOS 27, Apple expands Precision Finding on the Watch to AirPods Pro 3.

AirPods Pro 3’s case includes the latest second-generation Ultra Wideband (UWB) chip, letting you find it with greater precision and step-by-step guidance right from your wrist.

With every batch of upcoming AirPods features that debuts, the AirPods settings screen in the Settings app gets more cluttered.

But in iOS 27, Apple has a welcome fix: it’s redesigned and reorganized all AirPods settings.

Now, you’ll find AirPods settings organized into more categories and submenus, accompanied by colorful icons. It makes finding the right setting way easier and more intuitive than before.

#4112. Tech Report: 8 Most Perfect Superhero Highlights of the Last 15 Years, Ranked

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1679 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 8 Most Perfect Superhero Highlights of the Last 15 Years, Ranked

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1679 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Before superheroes took over cinema, they were extremely popular on television.
  • Whether they're from the likes of Marvel, DC Comics, or another studio, there have been some near-perfect superhero highlights to air on both streaming services and network television since 2011.
  • According to recent reports, when it comes to underrated television projects, one of the first projects DC Comics fans might think of is none other than Doom Patrol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before superheroes took over cinema, they were extremely popular on television. For decades, they've been staples of the medium and have delivered some astounding content. Specifically, in the last decade and a half, superhero fans have been treated to some astounding content that has kept them engaged from year to year.

Whether they're from the likes of Marvel, DC Comics, or another studio, there have been some near-perfect superhero highlights to air on both streaming services and network television since 2011. From animation to live-action, there are series that are about as close to perfect as one can get because of their writing, directing, visuals, and so much more.

According to recent reports, when it comes to underrated television projects, one of the first projects DC Comics fans might think of is none other than Doom Patrol. Despite being in the same universe as Titans—a notoriously rough show—Doom Patrol was a great experience for those who watched it. The series takes the traditions of a superhero television show and decides to do its own thing.

Industry observers note that doom Patrol decides to center itself around a group of absolute misfits who are filled to the brim with trauma and complex characters. The world within this show is also bizarre and owns it. The best part, though? Doom Patrol manages to take the wacky and wild world, their traumatized characters, and bring them together. The way the show balances these two contrasting things makes Doom Patrol feel layered.

Superhero media is always a blast to enjoy when it's written traditionally, but Harley Quinn proves that a well-written satire can be just as effective—sometimes even more so. The Batman/Gotham City corner of the DC Comics universe has always been treated in a very grounded, gritty, and dark manner, which is why Harley Quinn ends up being as fun as it is. Using such a typically gritty world, and turning it into complete satire, leaves this 2019 adult-humored animated series being extremely hilarious.

But, that's not the main reason that the story finds itself being a pretty much perfect show—although it is a big part of it. Harley Quinn isn't fully focused on only being funny, but delivers heartwarming storytelling, too. It has a genuinely sincere plot that reminds audiences that it's not always about making people giggle, but truly affecting them emotionally, as well. Because of this, people have grown quite attached to the characters and want to continue seeing them on screen.

Industry observers note that finishing up the trilogy of demonstrates that began in 2021 with WandaVision, Marvel Studios and Disney+'s VisionQuest has rapidly become a certified hit. Following whom was once known as "White Vision" (Paul Bettany), this 2026 installment depicts the synthezoid not only starting to discover himself, but coming in contact with one of his two sons from WandaVision, Tommy Shepherd/Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica). Not only that, but it features the return of the ever-popular villain, Ultron (James Spader).

Brought to life by directors Vincenzo Natali, Christopher J. Byrne, Terry Matalas, and Gandja Monteiro, VisionQuest's eight episodes weave together a phenomenal story. It doesn't just show the growth of Vision and Tommy, but highlights the entire origin of AIs in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as a whole — which includes the classic Human Torch (Paul Bettany) featured briefly in Captain America: The First Avenger. No one could have ever guessed that AIs had such a wild origin back when they first met J.A.R.V.I.S. (Paul Bettany) in Iron Man, but VisionQuest makes it feel natural and believable.

In a recent development, in the last decade, one of the most popular anime in the West has become the one and only My Hero Academia by Kohei Horikoshi. Taking place in a world where the majority of the population has powers—known also as "Quirks"—this animated adventure depicts a young, quirkless boy named Izuku Midoriya (Daiki Yamashita and Justin Briner) gaining the power of the world's strongest hero, All Might (Kenta Miyake and Christopher Sabat). It's a bona fide underdog story through and through.

The numerous awards that My Hero Academia has won over the years—this last season being a prime example—is already the proof in the pudding that this show is the real deal. The animation is top-tier, the storytelling has excellent pacing, the character arcs are stellar, and the voice acting from both the Japanese and English casts is unforgettable.

Four teams, four completely different reasons to put yourself in danger for strangers. This is the roster you actually belong on, what they would want from you, and what it would cost you to stay.

You belong where the stakes are largest and the personalities are loudest. This is a team of people who are all used to being the most important person in the room, which is exactly why it works and exactly why it keeps nearly falling apart.

In a recent development, you have never had the luxury of being thanked for this. The X-Men protect a world that has never once been comfortable with them existing, and something in you understands exactly why they keep doing it anyway.

In a recent development, you do not want colleagues, you want your people. The Titans are the team where the friendship came first and the world-saving turned up afterwards as an inconvenient side effect.

You are not asking who to trust. You worked out the answer a while ago and it was nobody in a cape. This is where you go once you have decided the people in charge need watching, and that nobody else is going to do it.

It has been revealed that back when Avengers: Endgame premiered in 2019, no one could have expected the Loki (Tom Hiddleston) that escaped the 2012 timeline to have birthed one of the best superhero television reveals ever made. Created by Michael Waldron, Loki is one of the most masterfully written superhero series in quite some time for numerous reasons that continue to prove why Loki is such a fan-favorite character.

Loki serves to be a great protagonist, giving Waldron the chance to truly delve into the concept of redemption in a way that is heartwarming and hopeful. Loki goes the distance by turning this classic villain into someone who is wholly relatable, cheer-worthy, and a true hero—arguably one of the best character arcs in the MCU, honestly. It also cannot be forgotten that the score, composed by Natalie Holt, is one of the best of the entire MCU franchise. Each track is mesmerizing, and it deserves all the praise it has gotten, and even more after that.

Some may think that a character as grand as Superman would be impossible to pull off on live-action network television. While that's more than a valid concern, given how straining network budgets can end up being, the unforgettable Superman & Lois managed to make a pretty much perfect Superman story with what they were given on a network like The CW. This show delivered not only a near-perfect Superman story, but one that feels incredibly unique among all the others in television and film.

Sources indicate that in Superman & Lois, Clark Kent (Tyler Hoechlin) is married to Lois Lane (Elizabeth Tulloch) and has two sons, Jordan (Alex Garfin) and Jonathan (Jordan Eslass and Michael Bishop). Fans get to watch as Clark navigates being both a father and Superman, while his family grapples with the struggle of one of noted sons getting powers of his own. Not to mention, for any fans of Inde Navarrette post-Obsession, this is one of her first major projects—playing Sarah Cushing—and, obviously, she kills it.

It's no secret that X-Men: The Animated Series is one of the most beloved animated series of all time. The impact it had on pop culture and the superhero medium as a whole rivals even that of Batman: The Animated Series. Few expected, however, that the show would somehow make a comeback. Thankfully, for X-Men fans everywhere, in 2024, they were treated to X-Men '97, which blew the world away by being the same level of quality as the original, somehow.

According to recent reports, this continuation show is a perfect blend of what made X-Men: The Animated Series great and what modern fans of the series appreciate, while, at the end of the day, still managing to feel unique. Almost the entire original cast returns, the animation is updated while still feeling akin to the first, and they manage to evolve the story, without requiring audiences to watch through the entirety of X-Men: The Animated Series to get it. It's arguably the perfect example of how to make a follow-up series like this.

It's been said time and time again, and it doesn't become any less true: Daredevil is a work of art. Netflix and Marvel's television smash hit still goes down in history as one of the best superhero shows of all time, and, honestly, some argue that it's one of Netflix's best projects as a whole. Daredevil is a grounded, gritty, and raw story about the Man Without Fear that is engaging the entire way through. It introduced fans to some of the most iconic superhero castings out there, such as Charlie Cox as Daredevil, Jon Bernthal as Punisher, and Vincent D'Onofrio as Wilson Fisk.

In a recent development, after this series ended with its third season in 2018, audiences begged to see these characters again, which, in turn, spurred Marvel Studios and Disney+ to bring them back with Daredevil: Born Again. The best thing about this 2015 show is that even when it's at its lowest, it's amazing. Creator, writer, and developer Drew Goddard did a phenomenal job at bringing this Marvel Comics star to the small screen. The way the characters are developed across each season, and the dynamics they have with each other, is of the highest quality. While the plot is engaging from start to finish and the crime-thriller of it all is amazing, it's these amazing, well-developed characters that really serve as the best aspects of the show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a turn of fate somehow sadder than Punch the Monkey’s isolation and crueler than the loss of Harambe, the Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday that the beloved, internet famous Nile hippopotamus, Fiona, has died at the age of 9.

It has been revealed that “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo remarked in a tribute Thursday. “We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are.”.

Recent findings suggest that last week, vets reported that Fiona swallowed a knit hat that was accidentally thrown into her enclosure. Several days after the incident, Fiona’s appetite declined and zookeepers started a variety of tests and 24-hour care, in the hopes that Fiona could pass the hat naturally. (Surgery is a rarely recommended suggestion for hippos due to its high risk.) But Fiona continued to decline, losing energy and fluids.

“Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover,” Thursday’s statement added. “Please keep her keepers and everyone who tried to help her in your thoughts as they try to navigate and come to terms with this shocking news. They are also, understandably, asking for space at this time.”  Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Bruno Mars Mourns His Father's Death: 'The Man That Taught Me Everything I Know' Pearl Jam Plan ‘Big-Boy Conversation’ About Latest Drummer YouTube Rejects U.K. Government’s Request to Take Down Russell Brand Video.

Fiona made history when she was born in 2017 as the first hippo born at the Cincinnati Zoo in over 53 years. (She was named after the Shrek character, princess Fiona, for the unique shape and size of her ears). Her mother, Bibi, was 17 at the time and went into labor early, delivering Fiona six weeks premature. Fiona was only 29 pounds and could not stand or nurse on her own.

Sources indicate that keepers and staff at the Cincinnati Zoo began documenting her growth on social media, drawing in millions of well-wishers and international fans as they watched the wobbling baby hippo fight to live and then begin to thrive. Even when Fiona reached adulthood, she remained a beloved internet icon known for her strength and resilience through seemingly insurmountable odds. Fiona was a fighter — even until the end.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (938 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Epic accuses Apple of withholding 122,000 documents, seeks daily fines

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the company complies.
  • As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.
  • It has been revealed that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in a new filing, Epic Games accuses Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions and asks the court to impose daily fines until the company complies. Here are the details.

As a result of the lawsuit Epic Games brought against Apple in 2020, Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in 2021 that Apple would have to, among other things, allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

It has been revealed that apple responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. This, in turn, led the court to find Apple in civil contempt for violating its injunction. Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn that ruling, a dispute that has now reached the Supreme Court.

At the same time, district court proceedings will determine what, if any, commission Apple may charge on purchases made through external payment links. Apple submitted its proposal on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, and Epic is expected to respond after Apple completes its document production.

In a new filing, however, Epic is accusing Apple of withholding more than 122,000 documents related to how it arrived at its proposed commission rates.

One of the many aspects of the ever-sprawling battle between Epic Games and Apple centers on document production.

In its new filing, Epic says Apple has repeatedly failed to produce documents detailing how it arrived at its proposed commission rates, accusing the manufacturer of withholding materials it deems irrelevant to the proceedings.

Epic argues that Apple previously used questionable claims of attorney-client privilege to withhold documents during the contempt proceedings, but has now changed tactics.

It has been revealed that apple does introduce one tactical change from its prior campaign of delay. Whereas during the contempt proceeding Apple used bogus claims of privilege to evade its discovery obligations, this time Apple withholds thousands of documents on bogus claims of irrelevance. For example, Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple says decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s upcoming CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness. Moreover, Apple claims that it completed its production from the files of these custodians, yet its production does not include a single substantive email discussing the rates Apple ultimately proposed; any notes or communications reflecting what occurred at any meeting where these rates were discussed or decided; any internal analysis of the financial or business impact of the proposed commissions; any App Store profit and loss statements; or any support for Apple’s assertion that its incremental link-out costs are “essentially zero.”.

Epic goes on to state that “Apple cannot be trusted to fix this problem on its own,” proposing instead that the court order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents matching the search terms agreed upon by both parties, regardless of whether Apple considers them relevant.

Under this proposal, Apple would still be allowed to review documents for attorney-client privilege, but it would be up to Epic to determine which of the remaining documents are relevant to the case. Epic argues that existing confidentiality protections would prevent it from using any of the information for purposes unrelated to the litigation.

According to recent reports, given Apple’s position, Epic respectfully submits that the Court should order Apple to produce to Epic all non-privileged documents that hit on the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms, so that Epic itself can sift the wheat from the chaff. Doing so will avoid further delays and place no burden on Apple. Moreover, doing so would not raise any of the concerns that required Special Master involvement in the prior proceeding, namely concerns around the production of privileged Apple information to Epic. Under Epic’s proposed remedy, Apple would be allowed to continue its review for privilege. For these reasons, Epic asks this Court to order Apple to produce all non-privileged documents that hit on any of the Parties’ agreed-upon search terms by December 2, 2026 (one week after Apple’s deadline to substantially complete production), irrespective of any relevance or responsiveness assessment.

Finally, though Epic does not propose a specific dollar amount, it “asks that the Court impose on Apple a daily monetary sanction for each day Apple fails to comply after December 2, 2026.”.

According to the court docket, a hearing on Epic’s motion was initially scheduled for November 24 before Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers. However, a latest order filed today, which has yet to be made public, refers the discovery dispute to a magistrate judge and includes a notice terminating deadlines and hearings.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which released only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple could see iPhone shipments rise 7% next year, giving it a 26% share of global smartphone shipments, according to a new report. Here are the details.

As detailed by AppleInsider, a new Morgan Stanley research report says Apple is poised to ship approximately 270 million iPhones in 2027, a 7% bump from 2026.

The forecast comes amid a change of pace for Apple, which released only the iPhone 18 Pro models and iPhone Duo this fall, with the rest of its iPhone lineup reportedly set to arrive early next year.

Morgan Stanley notes that this could push some purchases from late 2026 into 2027, contributing to the projected shipment growth without necessarily reflecting an increase in underlying demand.

The report also comes as Apple and the rest of the smartphone industry continue to grapple with rising memory and storage prices, though previous reports have suggested that Apple is better positioned than many of its competitors to absorb those costs.

Apple raised iPhone prices in September, after keeping them stable for much of the year while competitors had already introduced price hikes. In some cases, they raised prices more than once within a matter of months.

Sources indicate that back to the report, it notes that global smartphone shipments are expected to drop 5% next year, compared with a previous forecast of 3.6% growth. That mentioned, it’s still an improvement over the estimated 13.8% decline in 2026.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to Apple and the iPhone specifically, Morgan Stanley notes that consumer interest in upgrading has remained largely unchanged year over year, with 37% of iPhone owners saying they are extremely likely to upgrade within the next 12 months. That’s compared with 41% of smartphone owners overall, a figure that dropped by 2 percentage points year over year.

As for the market’s reaction to the iPhone Duo, Morgan Stanley found that 22% of non-iPhone customers surveyed expressed interest in switching to Apple’s foldable device, with that figure reaching 34% in China.

Importantly, Morgan Stanley’s survey was conducted after the iPhone Duo was unveiled, but before it introduced, so these figures reflect consumer interest rather than actual purchasing behavior.

Apple Intelligence was another factor examined in the survey, with Morgan Stanley concluding that AI features are becoming less important in driving iPhone upgrades, while factors such as battery life and upgrade eligibility are gaining importance.

Finally, Morgan Stanley found that Apple’s customer retention rate increased three percentage points to a record 93%, while its net switching rate improved to 12%.

Huawei was the only other major smartphone brand to show a positive and improving net switching rate, while Samsung and Google remained relatively neutral, and Xiaomi, Motorola, Honor, Oppo, and Vivo recorded negative rates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that select WhatsApp beta testers on iOS are now seeing an option to use the app’s own backup service as an alternative to iCloud. Here are the details.

A few months ago, WABetaInfo reported that WhatsApp was working on its own backup service as an alternative to the current method of backing up chats, which relies on Apple’s iCloud.

At the time, the feature wasn’t available even to beta testers, but WABetaInfo’s report provided details on how it would work, including 2GB of free storage, optional paid intends for larger backups, and mandatory end-to-end encryption for backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers.

Now, the site reports that some WhatsApp owners running the latest TestFlight build are seeing the option to switch from iCloud to WhatsApp’s own backup service, suggesting that a wider rollout may not be too far off.

According to recent reports, people can switch to WhatsApp cloud storage from the Chat backup screen. Here, users will have to choose the backup provider they want to use. If they choose WhatsApp, they will have to secure their backups using end-to-end encryption. Since encryption is mandatory, users cannot skip this step. However, they can choose a different method to encrypt their backups. For example, users can secure their backups using a 64-digit encryption key. Users who do not know what to choose can opt for the passkey, which is the default method WhatsApp recommends. After users complete the setup, they can back up their chat history on WhatsApp’s servers. WhatsApp keeps the backup on its servers for four months after a subscription expires. If users do not renew their subscription, WhatsApp deletes the backup permanently.

Importantly, the site notes that backups stored on WhatsApp’s servers cannot right now be used to restore chats across platforms, meaning owners switching from iPhone to Android, or vice versa, will still need to rely on WhatsApp’s built-in chat transfer feature.

Although the feature appears to be rolling out to beta testers first, the report notes that “the latest version available on the App Store is also compatible with this functionality,” meaning WhatsApp could theoretically enable it for users running the public version without requiring another app patch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • iFixit’s teardown of the latest Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair.
  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iFixit’s teardown of the latest Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also indicated that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Recent findings suggest that percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

Recent findings suggest that percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

10 Indicates Like 'MobLand' You Should Watch Next

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception.
  • While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family.
  • Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that crime dramas often attract massive stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

While families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other highlights mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

Another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's manufacturer town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the fresh sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated strategy to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

In a recent development, mobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Industry observers note that based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

In a recent development, tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he claims he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates newly introduced maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Manufacturer all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

Best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other demonstrates on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

Recent findings suggest that the great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

Adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a fresh adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fellas, is it emasculating to love your virtual girlfriend?
  • According to recent reports, after 13 years of buildup, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here.
  • This time things will feel a little different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fellas, is it emasculating to love your virtual girlfriend? Does buying her flowers make you a cuck? Why can’t you hire a prostitute in the murder and grand larceny game?

All great questions. Let us explore.

According to recent reports, after 13 years of buildup, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. The latest installment of the GTA franchise is unique in that gamers are playing both sides of Bonnie and Clyde style romance in Vice City. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos serve as the game’s main protagonists, with Lucia being the first playable female protagonist in the history of the franchise. Historically, GTA has represented culturally reprehensible instances of violence with what they say is a satire-heavy approach intended to exaggerate the criminal world they are depicting. Some of it — like killing prostitutes in order to steal their money in GTA III — has not aged as well as the rest of the franchise.

This time things will feel a little different. Keeping up the romance between Jason and Lucia is a huge component of the gameplay. They are not only romantically involved but partners in a criminal enterprise; your decisions in relation to each other affect the gameplay. But for a certain selection of male gamers stuck in the GTA of their youth — in which beating strippers and hiring sex workers were some of the first viral video game content of the internet age — the notion that they might have to be nice to a collection of pixels arranged in a female form was a step too far.

“What is this cuck simulator” Youtube streamer Asmongold — who combines gaming coverage with right wing commentary for an audience of over two million — complained on Thursday He covered his hands with his face and writhed dramatically after being prompted by the game to take clothing and groceries for Lucia — who is about to be released from prison — out of the trunk of his car and into their apartment.

“What are they doing to me bro,” he vented. “I’m a little errand boy bro.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

He went on to complain, just a few hours into the game, that Lucia “doesn’t even have any positive traits.”.

“She’s impulsive, stupid, jealous, she doesn’t understand her place in the relationship, she’s not skilled, she’s selfish, is emotionally manipulative,” so basically “there is no real redeeming quality about Lucia.”.

Some customers have complained of an early game quest that prompts players to buy flowers for Lucia who — again — has just been released from prison.

Industry observers note that “GTA 6 is insanely cucked,” Clavicular, the “looksmaxxing” streamer who has mutilated himself into a pantomime of attractiveness, wrote on X. “Half of the missions are jestermaxing and simping for girls.”.

GTA 6 is insanely cucked, half of the missions are jestermaxing and simping for girls.

Right wing commentator Stephen Crowder noted that you “can build your girl’s IKEA furniture, do her nails, and buy her flowers, but you can no longer pick up hookers,” in the game. “Listen, hookers and killing are bad, I agree. But this isn’t about the Left suddenly becoming moral, it’s just selectively enforcing their twisted version of morality,” he added. (It’s worth mentioning that Crowder got divorced in 2021, a fact that came to light after home surveillance video emerged of him apparently berating his pregnant wife about her not doing her “wifely things“.).

You, of course, don’t have to do small, nice things for Lucia. You can be inconsiderate, unattentive, and she will simply like you less. The concept is difficult to grasp for some. One post on X with over 1.8 million impressions said that because prostitution had been removed from the game “when you come home exhausted late at night, Lucia throws a fit and gives you the silent treatment. They’ve turned a game made for men into a full-on game that puts men down.”  Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Pearl Jam Plan ‘Substantial-Boy Conversation’ About New Drummer Bruno Mars Mourns His Father's Death: 'The Man That Taught Me Everything I Know' Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend.

GTA VI is challenging the notion that a female protagonist in a video game — a cultural medium where women represent half of the American market — can only be compelling to the consumer as an avatar for their desires and escapism, and not as an equal partner in a story where character development is interactive and moldable. It is the most ambitious open world game of the modern era, and — overall – has been received with overwhelming acclaim by critics and owners alike.

Fortunately, for most of us, the notion that doing small things for your partner helps improve a critical relationship is not confined to fantasy spaces, or virtual escapism. You can still rob stores, steal an old woman’s moped, or even take a jet ski ride with a dog. You can shoot up a bank and careen through car chases with Vice City PD. And if you’re so inclined, you can take a stroll on the beach with your latina baddie to recharge the next day. It’s a game folks, don’t forget to play.
