It has been revealed that it's been another excellent year for gaming with newly introduced hardware, accessories and so many essential new games that playing them all is practically impossible. If you're not immersed in the world of gaming, knowing what the best gaming gifts are can be extremely overwhelming.

That's why I've done the research for you. I'm one of Tom's Guide's gaming experts, and I've picked out a selection of gifts that any gamer would love to receive this year. I've got options with a range of prices, from affordable picks to premium products, with each broken down in simple categories.

Whether the gamer in your life plays on PC, PlayStation, Nintendo, Xbox or mobile, these are the best gaming gifts in 2026.

Looking for more gift inspiration? Check out our guide to the best holiday gifts.

Choose to follow your gaming destiny with the powerful Victus Gaming Laptop leading you to immersive, fun-filled experiences. Enjoy playing with great, stable performance with an Intel Core processor and NVIDIA GeForce RTX Laptop GPU. OMEN Gaming Hub's performance toolkit elevates play with software enhancements and personalized hardware control.

The Xbox Series X remains the pinnacle of Microsoft's console family. It's a powerful, chunky black box that can run the latest games at 4K resolution at 60 frames per second without breaking a sweat. Plus, Xbox Game Pass is the best subscription service in gaming. It also offers the most robust backwards compatibility features of any console, letting you experience classic games from every Xbox generation.

It has been revealed that thanks to unwelcome price hikes, the Xbox Series S isn't quite the budget-friendly machine it was once. Nevertheless, it's still the cheapest current-generation console on the market. It plays all the same games as its more powerful Xbox Series X sibling, but with some graphical sacrifices. It's a great pick if you don't want to spend eyewatering sums on a console, and is the cheapest way to play Grand Theft Auto VI in 2026 — which is an especially major selling point.

A second controller is always useful for co-op gaming on Xbox consoles. You could get the standard black or white model, but the Forza Horizon 6 Limited Edition is way snazzier. Released in conjunction with the latest Forza game, its neon-bright yellow/pink/blue color scheme celebrates the title's vast open-world map of Japan. It also features translucent plastic, which is clearly back in style in 2026.

The latest title in the Gears of War franchise is a prequel set during Emergence Day (aka E-Day), the fateful moment when the Locust hordes first attacked humanity. You play as series stalwart Marcus Fenix alongside his best buddy, Dom Santiago, and a fresh crew of COG soldiers battling on the front lines of this future war. In TG's Gears of War E-Day review, we gave it an 'Editor's Choice' award, calling it "the must-own Xbox exclusive of 2026.".

If the gamer in your life hasn't already picked up Grand Theft Auto VI, then they're probably asking for it for Christmas. It's the long-awaited return of the GTA franchise after 13 years. This blockbuster is set in Vice City and introduces the franchise's first playable female protagonist in the story mode. Note: this is a "code in box" edition; it doesn't come with a physical game disc.

According to recent reports, the PS5/PS5 Slim is the best-selling console of this generation and, in 2026, continues to make an excellent case for itself. Its library is overflowing with great games, many in 4K resolution at 60 frames per second. Its DualSense controller is packed with novel features, like haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Plus, PlayStation is proudly boasting that "PS5 is the best place to play" GTA 6. There's also the PS5 Pro, for those demanding the most powerful console, but finding the already pricey Pro in stock is very difficult at present.

Sony's latest official PlayStation headset is the PlayStation Pulse, not to be confused with the PlayStation Pulse 3D, which arrived back in November 2020 alongside the PS5 console. It's a slick wireless headset with a built-in microphone and full UI integration on PS5. Its look also mirrors the PS5's two-tone aesthetics, so it's a great buy for gamers who want their entertainment setup to match.

The DualSense controller is great, but if you want a proper "pro" pad, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited is designed to give competitive gamers an edge. Its biggest upgrade is the built-in display, which lets you customize any of its seven shortcuts on the fly, and it also sports TMR joysticks, dual-mode actuation triggers, and a docking station for easy charging. It's also compatible with PC.

In a recent development, PS5's major blockbuster exclusive for 2026 is Marvel's Wolverine, the latest superhero romp from Spider-Man developer Insomniac Games. It's quite repetitive, but it's essentially a playable summer blockbuster that does have its appeal. Just be aware, it's not one for younger gamers. Wolverine's claws are used for all manner of violence. Trust me, Wolverine earns its "M" rating.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI is not just the biggest game of 2026, but the most anticipated game of the whole decade. Sony and Rockstar have confirmed it'll "play best on PlayStation," making the PS5 the place to experience this open-world crime epic 13 years in the making. As with the Xbox version, this is a "code in box" edition, without a physical disc, but it gives you the full game, and an actual box is nicer to wrap than some digital store vouchers.

The Nintendo Switch 2 was recently voted the console you should buy in 2026 by the Tom's Guide staff, and it's not hard to see why. Like its predecessor, it's a hybrid system, letting you play on a TV or undock for portable play on its 7.9-inch LCD display. Now in its second year, the Switch 2's library has really swelled in size, which makes deciding what to play first quite a challenge.

The Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller is a must-have extra if you strategy to use your Switch 2 in TV Mode for extended periods. It's the best Switch 2 controller around, offering a traditional button layout, ludicrously long battery life, and even comes with two back buttons. The Joy-Con 2 controllers work well for portable play, but if your Switch 2 is docked, you'll want to play on a Pro pad.

In a recent development, the Nintendo Switch 2's internal storage fills up very fast, with some games requiring more than 50 GB to install. For a portable system, this is a major pain, as you don't want to be deleting and redownloading software all the time. Fortunately, this Samsung 256GB microSD Express Card gives the Switch 2 plenty of additional storage, and comes sporting a charming little Mario design.

According to recent reports, the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been remade for the Nintendo Switch 2, and in a word, it's stunning. This complete remake of the classic Nintendo 64 offers overhauled visuals, improved controls, and a few smart tweaks to make the timeless game even more modern. Ocarina of Time was considered a masterpiece back in 1998, and this latest version on Switch 2 has earned the same plaudits.

Recent findings suggest that if you want a Switch 2 game that the whole family can play this holiday season, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is my top pick. It's a part of the spiritual successor series to Wii Sports, offering a large collection of sports mini-games that use motion controls to mimic the real thing. It's approachable even for non-gamers, and is sure to delight players of all ages. Just don't blame me if it causes a few overly competitive rounds of virtual bowling.

Upgrade your mobile gaming with the excellent Backbone Pro controller. It turns your smartphone into a device resembling the Nintendo Switch 2, giving you greater control of your mobile gaming experience and saving you from trying to play AAA games on a touchscreen. It's super portable, and with 40 hours of battery, the Backbone Pro will always have juice when you need it.

Xbox celebrated its 25th Anniversary this year, leading to a slew of limited edition products; one of my favorites is this GameSir X5 Lite mobile controller. It's an officially licensed accessory that, just like the Backbone Pro, turns your smartphone into a proper portable gaming device. It comes decked out in an attractive colorway that's a nod to the classic Xbox green. Its more wallet-friendly price means some compromises, but it's a capable, cheaper pick compared to the Backbone Pro.

Sources indicate that the Steam Deck OLED lags behind its competition when it comes to internal components, but it's still among the finest portable gaming devices around. It's great for tearing through your Steam backlog or enjoying the best indie games around; just don't expect to be playing the latest 2026 releases on the Deck. Unfortunately, post-launch price hikes have made this a tougher recommendation. At $789 for the 512GB model, it's overpriced, but its overall quality gets it a nod in this roundup.

Sources indicate that if you've got very deep pockets (and can find it in stock), you could make somebody's holiday season by gifting them the cutting-edge Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20. It's an upgrade on the ROG Xbox Ally X, with a stellar OLED display and fantastic ergonomics. However, it's hard to get over the sticker shock of the price. It makes the Steam Deck look affordable, which is really saying something. This is only for a gamer in your life who has been positively saintly in 2026.

Industry observers note that the Evercade Nexus is a handheld device designed for those who love retro gaming. It includes a 5.89-inch IPS display, dual analogue sticks, and wireless headphone support. There's no digital store to download games; instead, it's compatible with more than 80 physical Evercade cartridges (that's 700+ games). To get your collection started, the Evercade Nexus comes bundled with the Banjo-Kazooie Double Pack, collecting a pair of classic 3D platformers on a single cartridge. It's a nostalgia gamer's perfect handheld system.

Industry observers note that the VR gaming boom never quite exploded. Even PlayStation seems to have given up on the PSVR 2. However, the Meta Quest 3S is still a great, more budget-friendly virtual reality headset. Ideal for a gamer who already has all console/PC hardware they need. It comes bundled with Golf+, a VR game that lets you step onto the green in the most immersive way possible outside of paying for an overinflated membership at your local golf club.

The music rhythm game genre is making a significant comeback this year thanks to Stage Tour. Taking inspiration from Guitar Hero and Rock Band, you play along to a setlist of more than 90 tracks either on a regular controller or for the full rockstar experience on a plastic Guitar. This $129 bundle includes the Stage Tour game and a Kramer Wireless Guitar Controller and is available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.

Industry observers note that lego has released a few gaming-themed sets this year, and while the Lego PlayStation 1 is very novel, my pick of the bunch is the Lego Donkey Kong Arcade machine, which recreates a classic arcade cabinet playing the game that introduced the world to Mario. It looks great on display and comes with a play feature that lets you simulate the game in motion, with Mario jumping over barrels.

Industry observers note that last Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Sources indicate that starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.99, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:.

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $30 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

It has been revealed that kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original released all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $39.99.

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails between $59.99 and $69.99 for a physical copy, but Nintendo is selling it for $39.99 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Industry observers note that super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally debuted on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The organization offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $39.99 before Black Friday.

It has been revealed that nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

In a recent development, nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo revealed a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo states that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in Fresh York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

In a recent development, yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apple today unveiled that App Store prices for apps and In-App Purchases will be adjusted in five countries starting December 3, following changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates. Here are the details.

In a latest post published on its developer portal, Apple today announced a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the tech giant, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple said that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Apple added that a fresh “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and enhancement their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple this week revealed the additional Siri AI usage you’ll get if you have an iCloud+ subscription. This ranges from doubled limits for a 200GB blueprint to 20 times for a 12TB plan.

However, the tech giant’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

Sources indicate that apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time. However, it did list the proportional increases you get with paid iCloud intends.

However, tucked away in the small print in the company’s support document are some exclusions. One of them is no surprise: EU countries.

In a recent development, siri AI isn’t available at all in the EU due to Apple’s perception of potential antitrust issues. Essentially, Apple believes that if it launches Siri AI there, it will be required to give competing AI services the same level of access to its devices. But three other countries are specifically excluded:.

Apple gives no explanation, simply saying:.

Increased access to Siri AI with iCloud+ is subject to Siri AI availability and is not available in Brazil, the EU, UK, or South Korea.

However, I have a strong suspicion about the reason.

What all three countries have in common is that they’ve taken a strong antitrust stance with Apple on a number of occasions over a range of issues.

It may be that Apple has genuine concerns about how regulators might respond if they effectively throw in free access to increased Siri AI usage. The company may fear that this would be viewed as anti-competitive by implicitly disadvantaging other AI services.

In a recent development, A less charitable take would be that Apple is firing a warning shot across the bows of these countries, seeking to communicate that there are consequences for what it views as attacks on its ecosystem. If customers are angered by missing out, Apple might be hoping that these feelings would be directed at regulators rather than the iPhone maker.

What’s your take? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

Industry observers note that “We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

In a recent development, democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also mentioned on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

  • In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw launched Moonlock on the Mac, the company described its new app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. People can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that reveals where apps are sending data and lets consumers block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the manufacturer says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Recent findings suggest that unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping consumers improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets consumers quickly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

As MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, users can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

Sources indicate that “When we introduced Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Industry observers note that blondie has delivered the latest offering from their upcoming album, High Noon, out Feb. 26.

Sources indicate that their latest single, “Come Back Home,” is buoyant and evocative, despite its forlorn lyrics longing for a place to settle down. Written by Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig of Lucius, who also contribute their vocal harmonies, the track began as a personal song before finding its way to Blondie. “We had been on tour for a few years, and wrote this song; a sort of reflection of being away for too long, and the ways in which distance and the road can mess with your mind and your relationships,” stated Wolfe and Laessig in a statement. Speaking about the opportunity to work with Blondie, they said: “We grew up with Debbie Harry as the ultimate female icon of punk, rock, and disco—paving a path for women in music, blending styles, and reimagining herself. We never dreamed a song of ours would become part of the Blondie story.”.

According to recent reports, blondie guitarist Chris Stein likens “Come Back Home” to the feeling of Alison Krauss’s “Down to the River to Pray” from the Coen Brothers’ 2000 tragicomedy O Brother, Where Art Thou? The Blondie single carries the “same haunting, almost spiritual quality, with a sense of simplicity and restraint,” stated Stein. Sources indicate that the track follows “Spectral Eyes,” the album’s Johnny Marr-penned lead single, which released in October and marked Blondie’s first newly introduced music since 2017’s Pollinator. High Noon, their first album in nine years, spans 13 tracks and includes “Heartbreak Kid,” written by Stein; “Sleepwalking,” penned by Glen Matlock; and “Man Who Had No Face,” co-written by Stein and frontwoman Debbie Harry. The band also revisits “Little Metal Drummer,” which was originally recorded by Blondie co-founding keyboardist Jimmy Destri for his solo debut, Heart On A Wall. Both Harry and co-founding drummer Clem Burke, who died in April 2025, performed on the 1981 original recording.

“This album is classic Blondie — an amalgamation of all our different influences and eras into something newly introduced,” Harry mentioned in a previous statement. “This music feels grounded in the present, shaped by who we are and how we’re living now.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL debuted on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial revision.

Industry observers note that on Android, this comes in the form of upcoming color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

Industry observers note that in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

#4064. Breaking: Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2892 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big challenges.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big challenges.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he indicates he has identified the next big shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Ng’s current efforts are focused on his company Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he claims can yield “small data” solutions to big concerns in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

The great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Andrew Ng: This is a substantial question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

According to recent reports, ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a newly introduced paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

Recent findings suggest that ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of users, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of customers.

Ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

According to recent reports, I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and mentioned, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing newly introduced here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

In a recent development, ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

The data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one manufacturer or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that highlighted up.

Recent findings suggest that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Sources indicate that ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from substantial data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

According to recent reports, when you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand new model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Sources indicate that ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having said that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For substantial data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

In a recent development, for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very swiftly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

According to recent reports, could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Recent findings suggest that ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Fresh tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an important piece of the puzzle.

According to recent reports, one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

Ng: In AI, data cleaning is crucial, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention promptly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

Recent findings suggest that for example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

In a recent development, ng: I think synthetic data is an notable tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Industry observers note that ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

“In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

Synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

In a recent development, to make these complications more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a firm approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

Ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

It has been revealed that how do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

Ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and upgrade the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Sources indicate that in the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion people. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Industry observers note that ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent new neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s crucial for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

In a recent development, ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print issue as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

Recent findings suggest that the AiPaper Reader was obviously inspired by the more established Boox Palma family (which also has a latest addition—the Boox Palma 3—which is much pricier and not on sale for the shopping holiday). It's got the same 6.13-inch screen, mimicking most smartphones, but with a black-and-white e-ink display that's far easier on the eyes than your iPhone or Android's bright OLED. Though it's at the moment far cheaper than the Palma 3, the AiPaper Reader has many of the same features, including 128GB of storage, Google Play compatibility, and mobile data when you insert a SIM card (though the Viwoods device does Boox one better: It's also a secret phone.) It also has a lot of smart AI integrations, if you like that sort of thing. (If you only want to use it to read books from Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and any other source you like, you can also just ignore it.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, leaker Ice Universe says Apple is currently developing four models of the 20th anniversary iPhone which we’ve been referring to as the iPhone 20. We’re expecting next year’s flagship models to be a radical new design with an all-glass appearance.

Why four models rather than two is unclear, but it seems possible Apple is testing two versions of both the Pro and the Pro Max to determine just how ambitious it can be with the final product ….

Didn’t the iPhone 6 or the iPhone 11 already have a curved front glass?

Recent findings suggest that ice Universe states that two of the four models have quad-curved glass backs and two have flat glass. They indicate that Apple has already had to ramp back its ambitions with the curvature.

Apple is right now developing four models in total: two with flat glass backs and two with quad-curved glass backs. Apple has been prototyping this quad-curved design for three years, making several revisions along the way—particularly regarding the glass curvature, which is still being refined. The earliest version had a very pronounced curve; it was later reduced somewhat.

It’s standard practice for Apple to develop multiple competing prototypes of upcoming devices, evaluating them for everything from usability and durability to ease of manufacturing.

Recent findings suggest that we’re expecting Apple to use a combination of ultra-thin bezels and curved glass to create the illusion of no bezels at all – a more sophisticated version of the effect seen on the Apple Watch. Today’s report states the bezels are around 1mm thick.

The curved edges on the quad-curved version are approximately 1mm wide. However, because the glass curves around all sides, when viewed straight on from the front, the bezel becomes nearly invisible, creating a near‑borderless appearance. The actual visual effect could be quite stunning.

In a recent development, we yesterday saw an AI-generated render of what the design could look like. It’s expected to be the biggest redesign of the standard iPhone since the iPhone X.
